437.title: Physical and Environmental Security Controls
437.content:
NOTE TITLE: [[Physical and Environmental Security Controls]]

METADATA:{"tags":["ISO27001","Controls"],"parent":"ISMS Index","created":"2026/02/03 16:12:33","modified":"2026/02/12 09:29:22","chunkId":"02 Knowledge/ISO/ISMS/Controls/Physical and Environmental Security Controls.md#0","heading":"Physical and Environmental Security Controls"}

NOTE BLOCK CONTENT:

Back to  [[Controls Index]]

# Physical and Environmental Security Controls

## Purpose

The purpose of these controls is to prevent unauthorized physical access, damage, interference, or disruption to information, information systems, and supporting facilities.

Physical and environmental security controls protect people, assets, and infrastructure against physical threats and environmental hazards.

---

## Scope

These controls apply to:

- All facilities within the scope of the ISMS
    
- Offices, data centers, server rooms, and secure areas
    
- Physical information assets and IT equipment
    
- Environmental conditions affecting information processing facilities
    
- Employees, contractors, visitors, and third parties
    

---

## Control References

- **ISO/IEC 27001:2022 - Annex A 7.1** - Physical security perimeters
    
- **ISO/IEC 27001:2022 - Annex A 7.2** - Physical entry controls
    
- **ISO/IEC 27001:2022 - Annex A 7.3** - Securing offices, rooms, and facilities
    
- **ISO/IEC 27001:2022 - Annex A 7.4** - Physical security monitoring
    
- **ISO/IEC 27001:2022 - Annex A 7.5** - Protecting against physical and environmental threats
    
- **ISO/IEC 27001:2022 - Annex A 7.6** - Working in secure areas
    

(Standard: **ISO/IEC 27001**)

---

## Policy Statement

Physical access to facilities, equipment, and information assets shall be restricted and controlled to prevent unauthorized access, damage, or interference.

Environmental risks to information processing facilities shall be identified and mitigated to maintain availability and safety.

---

## Physical Security Principles

The organization shall ensure that:

- Physical access is restricted based on authorization and business need
    
- Secure areas are clearly defined and protected
    
- Physical security measures are proportionate to risk and asset value
    
- Environmental risks are identified and mitigated
    

---

## Physical Security Perimeters

- Physical security perimeters shall be defined and maintained
    
- Perimeters may include:
    
    - Walls, doors, locks, fences
        
    - Controlled entry points
        
- Perimeters shall protect areas containing sensitive information or systems
    

---

## Physical Entry Controls

- Access to facilities and secure areas shall be controlled
    
- Entry controls may include:
    
    - Badges or access cards
        
    - Keys or biometric controls
        
    - Visitor registration systems
        
- Access rights shall be reviewed periodically
    

---

## Securing Offices, Rooms, and Facilities

- Offices and rooms containing sensitive assets shall be secured
    
- Doors and access points shall be locked when unattended
    
- Sensitive areas shall not be accessible to unauthorized persons
    

---

## Physical Security Monitoring

- Physical security monitoring shall be implemented where appropriate
    
- Monitoring may include:
    
    - CCTV systems
        
    - Intrusion detection or alarms
        
- Monitoring activities shall comply with legal and privacy requirements
    

---

## Environmental Protection

- Facilities shall be protected against environmental threats such as:
    
    - Fire
        
    - Flooding
        
    - Power failure
        
    - Temperature or humidity extremes
        
- Environmental controls may include:
    
    - Fire detection and suppression systems
        
    - Climate control
        
    - Uninterruptible power supplies (UPS)
        

---

## Equipment Protection

- Equipment shall be protected against physical damage or theft
    
- Measures may include:
    
    - Secure mounting or locking
        
    - Protection against unauthorized removal
        
- Equipment shall be maintained in accordance with manufacturer recommendations
    

---

## Working in Secure Areas

- Secure areas shall be accessible only to authorized personnel
    
- Activities in secure areas shall be monitored where appropriate
    
- Sensitive work shall be performed in a controlled manner
    

---

## Visitor Management

- Visitors shall be identified and recorded
    
- Visitors shall be escorted where required
    
- Visitor access shall be limited to authorized areas and durations
    

---

## Roles & Responsibilities

### Management

- Approve physical and environmental security measures
    
- Ensure adequate resources for facility protection
    

### Facility / IT Management

- Implement and maintain physical and environmental controls
    
- Monitor facility conditions and security systems
    

### Information Security Function

- Define physical security requirements
    
- Assess risks and compliance
    
- Support incident response and improvement
    

### All Personnel

- Comply with physical security procedures
    
- Challenge or report suspicious behavior
    

---

## Compliance & Enforcement

Failure to comply with physical and environmental security controls may result in:

- Increased risk of physical or information loss
    
- Disciplinary action
    
- Contractual or legal consequences
    

---

## Review & Maintenance

These controls shall be reviewed periodically to ensure:

- Continued effectiveness of physical and environmental protections
    
- Alignment with risk assessments and facility changes
    
- Compliance with legal, regulatory, and contractual requirements
    

---

## Related Controls

METADATA:{"tags":["ISO27001","Controls"],"parent":"ISMS Index","created":"2026/02/03 16:12:33","modified":"2026/02/12 09:29:22","chunkId":"02 Knowledge/ISO/ISMS/Controls/Network Security Management Controls.md#0","heading":"Network Security Management Controls"}

# Network Security Management Controls

## Purpose

The purpose of these controls is to ensure that networks and network services are protected against unauthorized access, misuse, disruption, and compromise.

Effective network security management supports the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of information by safeguarding data flows, networked systems, and communication paths.

---

## Scope

These controls apply to:

- All organizational networks and network services
    
- Wired, wireless, and virtual networks
    
- On- premises, cloud, and hybrid network environments
    
- Network devices, services, and communication links
    
- Internal, external, and third- party network connections
    

---

## Control References

- **ISO/IEC 27001:2022 - Annex A 8.20** - Network security
    
- **ISO/IEC 27001:2022 - Annex A 8.21** - Security of network services
    
- **ISO/IEC 27001:2022 - Annex A 8.22** - Segregation of networks
    

(Standard: **ISO/IEC 27001**)

---

## Policy Statement

Networks and network services shall be managed and protected to prevent unauthorized access, ensure secure communication, and maintain service availability.

Network security controls shall be proportionate to risk, system criticality, and information classification.

---

## Network Security Principles

The organization shall ensure that:

- Network access is restricted to authorized users, devices, and services
    
- Network traffic is protected against interception and manipulation
    
- Network architectures support segregation and least privilege
    
- Network security controls are documented, monitored, and reviewed
    

---

## Network Architecture & Design

- Network architectures shall be designed with security in mind
    
- Security considerations shall include:
    
    - Segmentation and isolation
        
    - Trust boundaries
        
    - Redundancy and resilience
        
- Network diagrams and documentation shall be maintained
    

---

## Network Access Control

- Access to networks shall be controlled and authorized
    
- Authentication and authorization mechanisms shall be applied where appropriate
    
- Network access rights shall be reviewed periodically
    
- Unauthorized devices or connections shall be prevented or detected
    

---

## Segregation of Networks

- Networks shall be logically or physically segregated based on:
    
    - System criticality
        
    - Information classification
        
    - Risk level
        
- Segregation may include:
    
    - VLANs or subnets
        
    - Firewalls or access control lists
        
    - Virtual network separation
        
- Management, user, and system networks shall be separated where feasible
    

---

## Security of Network Services

- Network services shall be provided securely and reliably
    
- Security controls may include:
    
    - Firewalls and gateways
        
    - Intrusion detection or prevention systems
        
    - Secure routing and switching configurations
        
- Security requirements shall be considered when using third- party network services
    

---

## Protection of Data in Transit

- Network communications shall be protected against interception and alteration
    
- Encryption shall be used where required by classification or risk assessment
    
- Secure communication protocols shall be enforced
    

---

## Wireless Network Security

- Wireless networks shall be secured using approved authentication and encryption mechanisms
    
- Guest or public wireless networks shall be segregated from internal networks
    
- Wireless access shall be monitored for unauthorized use
    

---

## Remote Access & External Connections

- Remote network access shall be authorized and controlled
    
- Secure remote access solutions shall be used
    
- External connections shall be documented and monitored
    

---

## Network Monitoring & Logging

- Network activity shall be logged and monitored where appropriate
    
- Monitoring shall support detection of:
    
    - Unauthorized access
        
    - Malicious activity
        
    - Network failures
        
- Network security events shall feed into incident management processes
    

---

## Roles & Responsibilities

### Network & System Owners

- Define network security requirements
    
- Approve network access and changes
    

### IT / Operations

- Implement and maintain network security controls
    
- Monitor network performance and security
    

### Information Security Function

- Define network security standards
    
- Review network risks and compliance
    
- Support incident response and improvement
    

---

## Compliance & Enforcement

Failure to comply with network security management controls may result in:

- Increased exposure to cyber threats
    
- Service disruption
    
- Disciplinary, contractual, or legal consequences
    

---

## Review & Maintenance

These controls shall be reviewed periodically to ensure:

- Continued effectiveness of network security measures
    
- Alignment with evolving threats and technologies
    
- Compliance with business, legal, and regulatory requirements
    

---

METADATA:{"tags":["ISO27001","Controls"],"parent":"ISMS Index","created":"2026/02/03 16:12:33","modified":"2026/02/12 09:29:22","chunkId":"02 Knowledge/ISO/ISMS/Controls/Information Classification and Handling Controls.md#0","heading":"Information Classification and Handling Controls"}

NOTE BLOCK CONTENT:

Back to  [[Controls Index]]

# Information Classification and Handling Controls

## Purpose

The purpose of these controls is to ensure that information is classified and handled according to its value, sensitivity, and criticality, in order to protect it from unauthorized disclosure, modification, loss, or destruction.

Consistent classification and handling enable appropriate security controls to be applied throughout the information lifecycle.

---

## Scope

These controls apply to:

- All information created, processed, stored, or transmitted by the organization
    
- Information in all forms, including digital, physical, and verbal
    
- Information handled by employees, contractors, and third parties
    
- On- premises, cloud, remote, and third- party environments
    

---

## Control References

- **ISO/IEC 27001:2022 - Annex A 5.12** - Classification of information
    
- **ISO/IEC 27001:2022 - Annex A 5.13** - Labelling of information
    
- **ISO/IEC 27001:2022 - Annex A 8 (multiple controls)** - Secure handling, storage, and transmission
    

(Standard: **ISO/IEC 27001**)

---

## Policy Statement

Information shall be classified based on its sensitivity, value, and criticality, and handled in accordance with defined classification and handling requirements throughout its lifecycle.

Classification and handling rules shall be clearly communicated and consistently applied.

---

## Information Classification Principles

The organization shall ensure that:

- Information is classified in a consistent and understandable manner
    
- Classification reflects confidentiality, integrity, and availability requirements
    
- Protection measures are proportionate to risk
    
- Classification is reviewed and updated when information or context changes
    

---

## Classification Levels

Classification levels shall be defined and documented.  
Typical examples may include:

- **Public** - Information approved for public disclosure
    
- **Internal** - Information intended for internal use only
    
- **Confidential** - Sensitive business or personal information
    
- **Restricted** - Highly sensitive or critical information
    

The number and naming of levels may be adapted to organizational needs.

---

## Information Ownership

- Each information asset shall have a designated owner
    
- Information owners are responsible for:
    
    - Assigning and reviewing classification
        
    - Defining handling requirements
        
    - Approving access and sharing
        

---

## Labelling of Information

- Information shall be labelled where appropriate to reflect its classification
    
- Labelling may be applied:
    
    - Digitally (metadata, headers, footers)
        
    - Physically (paper documents, media labels)
        
- Where labelling is not feasible, alternative measures shall be applied
    

---

## Information Handling Requirements

Handling requirements shall be defined based on classification and may include controls for:

### Storage

- Approved storage locations and systems
    
- Encryption or physical protection requirements
    

### Access

- Access restrictions based on need- to- know
    
- Monitoring of access to sensitive information
    

### Transmission

- Secure transmission mechanisms
    
- Restrictions on external sharing
    

### Processing

- Approved tools and environments
    
- Protection against unauthorized modification
    

---

## Handling in Different Environments

### Physical Environments

- Secure storage of paper documents and removable media
    
- Controlled access to offices and storage areas
    

### Digital Environments

- Logical access controls
    
- Encryption where required
    
- Secure configuration of systems
    

### Remote & Mobile Working

- Additional safeguards for portable devices
    
- Protection against unauthorized viewing or access
    

---

## Information Sharing & Disclosure

- Information sharing shall be:
    
    - Authorized
        
    - Purpose- limited
        
    - Proportionate to risk
        
- Sharing with third parties shall comply with contractual and security requirements
    

---

## Reclassification & Declassification

- Information classification shall be reviewed periodically
    
- Reclassification shall occur when:
    
    - Information sensitivity changes
        
    - Business or legal requirements change
        
- Declassification shall be documented where appropriate
    

---

## Roles & Responsibilities

### Information Owners

- Classify and review information
    
- Define handling requirements
    

### Users

- Handle information according to its classification
    
- Apply labelling and protection measures
    
- Report suspected misclassification or mishandling
    

### Information Security Function

- Define classification and handling standards
    
- Support awareness and training
    
- Monitor compliance
    

---

## Compliance & Enforcement

Failure to comply with classification and handling requirements may result in:

- Increased risk of information disclosure
    
- Disciplinary action
    
- Contractual or legal consequences
    

---

## Review & Maintenance

These controls shall be reviewed periodically to ensure:

- Continued alignment with business and risk context
    
- Effectiveness of classification and handling rules
    
- Consistency with other ISMS controls
    

---

440.title: Malware and Antivirus Controls
440.content:
NOTE TITLE: [[Malware and Antivirus Controls]]

METADATA:{"tags":["ISO27001","Controls"],"parent":"ISMS Index","created":"2026/02/03 16:12:33","modified":"2026/02/12 09:29:22","chunkId":"02 Knowledge/ISO/ISMS/Controls/Malware and Antivirus Controls.md#0","heading":"Malware and Antivirus Controls"}

NOTE BLOCK CONTENT:

Back to  [[Controls Index]]

# Malware and Antivirus Controls

## Purpose

The purpose of these controls is to protect information systems and information assets against malware, including viruses, ransomware, spyware, and other malicious code.

Effective malware protection reduces the risk of system compromise, data loss, service disruption, and unauthorized access.

---

## Scope

These controls apply to:

- All systems, endpoints, servers, and devices within ISMS scope
    
- Workstations, servers, mobile devices, and virtual environments
    
- On- premises, cloud, and third- party hosted systems
    
- All users, including employees, contractors, and third parties
    

---

## Control Reference

- **ISO/IEC 27001:2022 - Annex A 8.7** - Protection against malware
    

(Standard: **ISO/IEC 27001**)

---

## Policy Statement

Appropriate measures shall be implemented to prevent, detect, and respond to malware infections in a timely and effective manner.

Malware protection controls shall be proportionate to risk, system criticality, and threat landscape.

---

## Malware Protection Principles

The organization shall ensure that:

- Malware protection is implemented across all relevant systems
    
- Protection mechanisms are kept up to date
    
- Malware risks are reduced through both technical and organizational measures
    
- Users are aware of malware threats and safe computing practices
    

---

## Anti- Malware Software

- Anti- malware solutions shall be deployed on systems where appropriate
    
- Anti- malware software shall:
    
    - Be enabled and active
        
    - Receive regular updates
        
    - Operate with real- time protection where feasible
        
- Tampering with or disabling malware protection is prohibited unless formally authorized
    

---

## Malware Detection & Prevention Measures

Measures may include:

- Real- time scanning of files and processes
    
- Scanning of removable media
    
- Email and web content scanning
    
- Network- based malware detection
    
- Application control or allowlisting
    

Controls shall be selected based on risk and system role.

---

## Updates & Signatures

- Malware detection engines and signatures shall be kept up to date
    
- Updates shall be applied automatically where feasible
    
- Failures in updating shall be monitored and addressed
    

---

## User Responsibilities & Safe Practices

Users shall:

- Avoid opening suspicious attachments or links
    
- Use only approved software and systems
    
- Report suspected malware or unusual system behavior immediately
    

Users shall **not**:

- Install unauthorized software
    
- Disable malware protection controls
    
- Connect unapproved removable media
    

---

## Handling Malware Incidents

- Suspected or confirmed malware infections shall be treated as security incidents
    
- Affected systems shall be:
    
    - Isolated where necessary
        
    - Investigated
        
    - Cleaned, restored, or rebuilt as appropriate
        
- Lessons learned shall be used to improve controls
    

---

## Malware Protection in Special Environments

### Servers & Critical Systems

- Malware protection shall be compatible with system performance and availability requirements
    
- Exclusions shall be documented and approved
    

### Cloud & Virtual Environments

- Malware protection responsibilities shall be clearly defined
    
- Platform- native protections may be used where appropriate
    

### Removable Media

- Use of removable media shall be controlled
    
- Media shall be scanned prior to use
    

---

## Roles & Responsibilities

### Users

- Follow safe computing practices
    
- Report suspected malware incidents
    

### IT / Operations

- Deploy and maintain malware protection solutions
    
- Monitor malware alerts and system status
    

### Information Security Function

- Define malware protection requirements
    
- Review malware risks and trends
    
- Coordinate response and improvement activities
    

---

## Monitoring & Compliance

- Malware protection status shall be monitored
    
- Alerts and detections shall be reviewed
    
- Non- compliance or control failures shall be addressed
    

---

## Review & Maintenance

These controls shall be reviewed periodically to ensure:

- Continued effectiveness against evolving threats
    
- Alignment with system architectures and risks
    
- Integration with incident management and monitoring processes
    

---

## Related Controls

- [[Incident management controls]]
    
- [[Access Control Controls]]

METADATA:{"tags":["ISO27001","Controls"],"parent":"ISMS Index","created":"2026/02/03 16:12:33","modified":"2026/02/12 09:29:22","chunkId":"02 Knowledge/ISO/ISMS/Controls/Logging and Monitoring Controls.md#0","heading":"Logging and Monitoring Controls"}

# Logging and Monitoring Controls

## Purpose

The purpose of these controls is to ensure that security- relevant events are logged, monitored, and reviewed to detect unauthorized activities, security incidents, system failures, and policy violations in a timely manner.

Effective logging and monitoring support incident detection, investigation, compliance, and continual improvement of information security.

---

## Scope

These controls apply to:

- All systems, applications, networks, and infrastructure within ISMS scope
    
- On- premises, cloud, and third- party hosted environments
    
- Security- relevant events, activities, and system behaviors
    
- Logs generated by users, administrators, applications, and security controls
    

---

## Control References

- **ISO/IEC 27001:2022 - Annex A 8.15** - Logging
    
- **ISO/IEC 27001:2022 - Annex A 8.16** - Monitoring activities
    

(Standard: **ISO/IEC 27001**)

---

## Policy Statement

Security- relevant events shall be logged and monitored to enable timely detection of threats, investigation of incidents, and verification of control effectiveness.

Logging and monitoring activities shall be proportionate to risk, system criticality, and information sensitivity.

---

## Logging Principles

The organization shall ensure that:

- Logs provide sufficient detail to support investigation and auditing
    
- Logs are accurate, complete, and protected against tampering
    
- Logging is enabled by default on critical systems
    
- Logging activities respect legal, regulatory, and privacy requirements
    

---

## Events to Be Logged

Security- relevant events may include, where applicable:

- User authentication and authorization events
    
- Privileged access and administrative actions
    
- System configuration changes
    
- Access to sensitive or restricted data
    
- Security control alerts and failures
    
- Application and system errors
    
- Network and firewall events
    

The specific events logged shall be defined based on risk and system role.

---

## Log Protection & Integrity

- Logs shall be protected against:
    
    - Unauthorized access
        
    - Modification or deletion
        
    - Loss or destruction
        
- Access to logs shall be restricted based on least privilege
    
- Log integrity mechanisms shall be used where appropriate
    

---

## Centralized Logging

- Logs from critical systems shall be centralized where feasible
    
- Centralized logging shall support:
    
    - Correlation of events
        
    - Efficient monitoring and analysis
        
    - Incident investigation
        

---

## Monitoring Activities

- Logged events shall be monitored to identify:
    
    - Suspicious behavior
        
    - Policy violations
        
    - Indicators of compromise
        
    - Operational failures
        
- Monitoring may be:
    
    - Automated
        
    - Manual
        
    - Risk- based
        

---

## Alerting & Response

- Alerts shall be generated for significant or high- risk events
    
- Alert thresholds and escalation paths shall be defined
    
- Monitoring outputs shall feed into incident management processes
    

---

## Log Retention

- Log retention periods shall be defined and documented
    
- Retention shall consider:
    
    - Legal and regulatory requirements
        
    - Investigation and audit needs
        
    - Storage and performance considerations
        
- Logs shall be securely deleted or archived when retention periods expire
    

---

## Privacy & Legal Considerations

- Logging and monitoring shall comply with applicable privacy and labor regulations
    
- Monitoring shall be proportionate and transparent where required
    
- Access to personal data within logs shall be restricted and justified
    

---

## Roles & Responsibilities

### System & Service Owners

- Define logging requirements for their systems
    
- Ensure logging is enabled and appropriate
    

### IT / Operations

- Implement and maintain logging and monitoring solutions
    
- Ensure log collection, storage, and availability
    

### Information Security Function

- Define logging and monitoring standards
    
- Review monitoring outputs and trends
    
- Support incident investigation and improvement activities
    

---

## Monitoring Effectiveness

- Logging and monitoring effectiveness shall be reviewed periodically
    
- Reviews may consider:
    
    - Incident detection performance
        
    - False positives and missed events
        
    - Audit findings
        
- Improvements shall be implemented where gaps are identified
    

---

## Compliance & Enforcement

Failure to comply with logging and monitoring controls may result in:

- Reduced ability to detect incidents
    
- Increased security risk
    
- Audit findings or compliance issues
    

---

## Review & Maintenance

These controls shall be reviewed periodically to ensure:

- Continued effectiveness
    
- Alignment with evolving threats and technologies
    
- Compliance with legal, regulatory, and contractual requirements
    

---

## Related Controls

- [[Access Control Controls]]
    
- [[Change Management Controls]]
    
- [[Cryptographic Control and Encryption Controls]]
    
- [[Data Protection Controls]]

442.content:
NOTE TITLE: [[Information Transfer Controls]]

METADATA:{"tags":["ISO27001","Controls"],"parent":"ISMS Index","created":"2026/02/03 16:12:33","modified":"2026/02/12 09:29:22","chunkId":"02 Knowledge/ISO/ISMS/Controls/Information Transfer Controls.md#0","heading":"Information Transfer Controls"}

Back to  [[Controls Index]]

# Information Transfer Controls

## Purpose

The purpose of these controls is to ensure that information transferred within the organization and to external parties is protected against unauthorized access, disclosure, alteration, loss, or misuse.

Effective information transfer controls reduce the risk of data leakage and ensure that information is exchanged securely and appropriately.

---

## Scope

These controls apply to:

- All forms of information transfer
    
- Digital, physical, and verbal information exchanges
    
- Internal and external information transfers
    
- Transfers involving employees, contractors, and third parties
    
- On- premises, cloud, and remote working environments
    

---

## Control Reference

- **ISO/IEC 27001:2022 - Annex A 5.14** - Information transfer
    

(Standard: **ISO/IEC 27001**)

---

## Policy Statement

Information shall be transferred in a manner that maintains its confidentiality, integrity, and availability, in accordance with its classification and applicable legal, regulatory, and contractual requirements.

Information transfer methods and controls shall be appropriate to the sensitivity and risk associated with the information being exchanged.

---

## Information Transfer Principles

The organization shall ensure that:

- Information is transferred only for authorized and legitimate purposes
    
- Transfer methods are appropriate to the information classification
    
- Information is protected during transmission and delivery
    
- Responsibilities for information protection are clearly defined
    

---

## Approved Transfer Methods

- Approved methods for information transfer shall be defined and documented
    
- Transfer methods may include:
    
    - Secure electronic communication channels
        
    - Encrypted file transfer mechanisms
        
    - Approved collaboration platforms
        
    - Secure physical media transfer
        

Unapproved or insecure transfer methods shall not be used for sensitive information.

---

## Information Classification & Transfer

- Information shall be classified prior to transfer
    
- Classification shall determine:
    
    - Whether transfer is permitted
        
    - Approved transfer methods
        
    - Required protection measures (e.g. encryption)
        
- Highly sensitive information may require additional authorization prior to transfer
    

---

## Secure Electronic Transfer

- Information transferred electronically shall be protected against interception or alteration
    
- Secure communication protocols shall be used where required
    
- Authentication and access controls shall be applied to transfer mechanisms
    

---

## Physical Media Transfer

- Physical media containing information shall be protected during transport
    
- Media shall be:
    
    - Appropriately labelled where required
        
    - Tracked and controlled
        
    - Protected against loss or theft
        
- Secure disposal shall be applied after use
    

---

## Verbal Information Transfer

- Sensitive information shared verbally shall be protected against unauthorized disclosure
    
- Care shall be taken in public or shared environments
    
- Verbal disclosure shall be limited to authorized recipients
    

---

## Information Transfer to Third Parties

- Transfers to third parties shall be:
    
    - Authorized
        
    - Documented
        
    - Limited to defined purposes
        
- Information transfer requirements shall be addressed in contracts or agreements
    
- Third- party recipients shall implement appropriate protection measures
    

---

## Information Receipt & Verification

- Received information shall be verified where appropriate to ensure:
    
    - Completeness
        
    - Accuracy
        
    - Integrity
        
- Unexpected or suspicious information transfers shall be reported
    

---

## Logging & Monitoring

- Information transfer activities may be logged where appropriate
    
- Logs shall support monitoring, investigation, and audit requirements
    
- Anomalies or failures in transfer controls shall be investigated
    

---

## Roles & Responsibilities

### Information Owners

- Approve information transfers
    
- Define transfer and protection requirements
    

### Users

- Use approved transfer methods
    
- Protect information during transfer
    
- Report incidents or suspected data leakage
    

### IT / Operations

- Implement secure transfer mechanisms
    
- Monitor and maintain transfer systems
    

### Information Security Function

- Define information transfer standards
    
- Monitor compliance
    
- Support incident response and improvement
    

---

## Compliance & Enforcement

Failure to comply with information transfer controls may result in:

- Increased risk of information disclosure
    
- Disciplinary action
    
- Contractual or legal consequences
    

---

## Review & Maintenance

These controls shall be reviewed periodically to ensure:

- Continued effectiveness of transfer mechanisms
    
- Alignment with information classification and risk
    
- Compliance with legal, regulatory, and contractual requirements
    

---

## Related Controls

# Information Security Awareness and Training Controls

## Purpose

The purpose of these controls is to ensure that personnel are aware of information security risks, responsibilities, and required behaviors, and that they possess the necessary competence to perform their roles securely.

Effective awareness and training reduce the likelihood of human error, policy violations, and security incidents.

---

## Scope

These controls apply to:

- All employees, contractors, interns, and temporary staff
    
- Third parties with access to organizational information or systems
    
- All roles within the scope of the Information Security Management System (ISMS)
    

---

## Control References

- **ISO/IEC 27001:2022 - Clause 7.2** - Competence
    
- **ISO/IEC 27001:2022 - Clause 7.3** - Awareness
    

(Standard: **ISO/IEC 27001**)

---

## Policy Statement

All personnel shall receive appropriate information security awareness and training to ensure they understand their responsibilities and can perform their duties in a secure and compliant manner.

Awareness and training activities shall be proportionate to role, risk, and access to information assets.

---

## Awareness Objectives

Information security awareness activities shall ensure that personnel understand:

- The importance of information security
    
- Relevant information security policies and procedures
    
- Their individual responsibilities for protecting information
    
- How to recognize and report security incidents
    
- The consequences of non- compliance
    

---

## Training Requirements

### General Awareness Training

- All personnel shall receive baseline information security awareness training
    
- Training shall cover topics such as:
    
    - Acceptable use
        
    - Password and authentication practices
        
    - Phishing and social engineering
        
    - Data protection and classification
        
    - Incident reporting
        

---

### Role- Based Training

- Additional training shall be provided for roles with increased security responsibility, such as:
    
    - IT and system administrators
        
    - Developers
        
    - Managers and asset owners
        
- Role- based training shall address specific risks and controls relevant to the role
    

---

### Specialized Training

- Specialized training shall be provided where required, such as:
    
    - Secure development practices
        
    - Incident response procedures
        
    - Regulatory or compliance obligations
        

---

## Training Delivery & Frequency

- Awareness and training may be delivered through:
    
    - Instructor- led sessions
        
    - E- learning platforms
        
    - Workshops or simulations
        
    - Awareness campaigns
        
- Awareness activities shall be conducted periodically
    
- Training shall be refreshed at planned intervals and upon significant change
    

---

## Onboarding & Changes

- Information security awareness shall be included in onboarding processes
    
- Additional training shall be provided when:
    
    - Roles or responsibilities change
        
    - New systems or significant risks are introduced
        

---

## Awareness Reinforcement

- Ongoing awareness may be reinforced through:
    
    - Communications and reminders
        
    - Posters or internal messaging
        
    - Phishing simulations or exercises
        
- Awareness materials shall remain relevant and up to date
    

---

## Roles & Responsibilities

### Management

- Promote a culture of information security awareness
    
- Ensure resources for training and awareness activities
    

### Information Security Function

- Define awareness and training requirements
    
- Develop or approve training content
    
- Monitor effectiveness of awareness activities
    

### Human Resources

- Support onboarding and role- based training processes
    
- Maintain training records
    

### Personnel

- Participate in required awareness and training activities
    
- Apply learned practices in daily work
    

---

## Records & Evidence

- Records of training and awareness activities shall be maintained
    
- Records may include:
    
    - Attendance logs
        
    - Completion certificates
        
    - Training materials
        
- Records shall be retained in accordance with retention requirements
    

---

## Monitoring & Effectiveness

- Effectiveness of awareness and training shall be evaluated through:
    
    - Assessments or quizzes
        
    - Incident trends
        
    - Audit findings
        
- Results shall be used to improve awareness and training programs
    

---

## Compliance & Enforcement

Failure to complete required training or comply with awareness requirements may result in:

- Access restrictions
    
- Disciplinary action
    
- Contractual consequences
    

---

## Review & Maintenance

These controls shall be reviewed periodically to ensure:

- Continued relevance to risks and roles
    
- Effectiveness of awareness and training activities
    
- Alignment with ISMS objectives
    

---

## Related Controls

- [[Access Control Controls]]
    
-[[Incident Management Controls]]

444.content:

METADATA:{"tags":["ISO27001","Controls"],"parent":"ISMS Index","created":"2026/02/03 16:12:33","modified":"2026/02/12 09:29:22","chunkId":"02 Knowledge/ISO/ISMS/Controls/Information Security Controls.md#0","heading":"Information Security Controls"}

NOTE BLOCK CONTENT:

Back to  [[Controls Index]]

# Information Security Controls

## Purpose

The purpose of these controls is to establish, implement, maintain, and continually improve an effective framework for managing information security risks and protecting information assets.

Information security controls ensure the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of information in alignment with business objectives, legal and regulatory requirements, and risk tolerance.

---

## Scope

These controls apply to:

- The entire Information Security Management System (ISMS)
    
- All information assets within the ISMS scope
    
- All organizational units, processes, systems, and services
    
- All employees, contractors, and third parties with access to information
    

---

## Control References

- **ISO/IEC 27001:2022 - Clauses 4-10** - ISMS requirements
    
- **ISO/IEC 27001:2022 - Annex A** - Information security controls
    

(Standard: **ISO/IEC 27001**)

---

## Policy Statement

The organization shall implement appropriate organizational, people, physical, and technological information security controls based on risk assessment and treatment to protect information assets against threats and vulnerabilities.

Information security controls shall be documented, implemented, monitored, reviewed, and continually improved.

---

## Information Security Objectives

Information security controls shall support the following objectives:

- Protect information from unauthorized access or disclosure
    
- Prevent unauthorized modification or destruction of information
    
- Ensure information and systems are available when required
    
- Maintain trust with customers, partners, and stakeholders
    
- Meet legal, regulatory, and contractual obligations
    

---

## Control Framework

Information security controls are structured and applied across the following domains:

### Organizational Controls

- Policies, procedures, and governance structures
    
- Asset management
    
- Supplier and third- party security
    
- Incident and continuity management
    

### People Controls

- Awareness and training
    
- Acceptable use
    
- Clear desk and clear screen
    
- Human resource security
    

### Physical Controls

- Physical access controls
    
- Protection of facilities and equipment
    

### Technological Controls

- Access control and identity management
    
- Cryptographic and encryption controls
    
- Backup and recovery
    
- Logging, monitoring, and secure configuration
    

---

## Risk- Based Control Selection

- Information security controls shall be selected based on:
    
    - Risk assessments
        
    - Business requirements
        
    - Information classification
        
    - Legal and regulatory obligations
        
- Controls shall be proportionate to the identified risks
    
- Residual risks shall be accepted or treated in accordance with defined criteria
    

---

## Implementation & Integration

- Information security controls shall be:
    
    - Documented and approved
        
    - Integrated into business processes and systems
        
    - Communicated to relevant stakeholders
        
- Controls shall be implemented consistently across the organization
    

---

## Monitoring & Measurement

- The effectiveness of information security controls shall be monitored
    
- Metrics and indicators may be used to:
    
    - Assess control performance
        
    - Identify trends and weaknesses
        
- Results shall be reviewed and used to drive improvements
    

---

## Incident Handling & Control Failures

- Failures or weaknesses in information security controls shall be:
    
    - Identified
        
    - Reported
        
    - Investigated
        
- Control failures may result in corrective actions, improvements, or risk reassessment
    

---

## Roles & Responsibilities

### Management

- Provide leadership and support for information security
    
- Approve policies and objectives
    
- Ensure adequate resources
    

### Information Security Function

- Define and maintain information security controls
    
- Monitor compliance and effectiveness
    
- Coordinate improvement activities
    

### Asset & Process Owners

- Ensure controls are applied within their areas of responsibility
    

### All Personnel

- Comply with information security controls
    
- Protect information assets
    
- Report security incidents or weaknesses
    

---

## Compliance & Enforcement

Non- compliance with information security controls may result in:

- Increased security risk
    
- Disciplinary measures
    
- Contractual or legal consequences
    

---

## Review & Continual Improvement

Information security controls shall be reviewed periodically to ensure:

- Continued suitability and effectiveness
    
- Alignment with business objectives and risks
    
- Incorporation of lessons learned and best practices
    

---

## Related Controls & Documents

- [[Asset Management Controls]]
    
- [[Access Control Controls]]
    
- [[Data Protection Controls]] & [[Data Retention Controls]]
    
- [[Incident Management Controls]]

NOTE TITLE: [[Incident Management Controls]]

METADATA:{"tags":["ISO27001","Controls"],"parent":"ISMS Index","created":"2026/02/05 09:52:45","modified":"2026/02/12 09:29:22","chunkId":"02 Knowledge/ISO/ISMS/Controls/Incident Management Controls.md#0","heading":"Incident Management Controls"}

NOTE BLOCK CONTENT:

Back to  [[Controls Index]]

# Incident Management Controls

## Purpose

The purpose of these controls is to ensure that information security incidents are identified, reported, assessed, responded to, and resolved in a consistent and timely manner, minimizing impact to the organization.

Effective incident management supports rapid containment, recovery, learning, and continual improvement of information security.

---

## Scope

These controls apply to:

- All information security incidents and suspected incidents
    
- All employees, contractors, and third parties
    
- All systems, applications, networks, and information assets
    
- Incidents occurring internally or involving third parties
    

---

## Control References

- **ISO/IEC 27001:2022 - Annex A 5.24** - Information security incident management planning and preparation
    
- **ISO/IEC 27001:2022 - Annex A 5.25** - Assessment and decision on information security events
    
- **ISO/IEC 27001:2022 - Annex A 5.26** - Response to information security incidents
    
- **ISO/IEC 27001:2022 - Annex A 5.27** - Learning from information security incidents
    
- **ISO/IEC 27001:2022 - Annex A 5.28** - Collection of evidence
    

(Standard: **ISO/IEC 27001**)

---

## Policy Statement

Information security incidents and events shall be reported, assessed, managed, and resolved in a timely, structured, and coordinated manner.

The organization shall learn from incidents to reduce the likelihood and impact of future occurrences.

---

## Incident Management Principles

The organization shall ensure that:

- Personnel know how and when to report incidents
    
- Security events are assessed consistently
    
- Incidents are handled proportionate to their severity and impact
    
- Responsibilities and escalation paths are clearly defined
    
- Lessons learned are captured and acted upon
    

---

## Definition of Events and Incidents

- **Information security event**: An observed occurrence that may affect information security
    
- **Information security incident**: One or more events that compromise, or threaten to compromise, confidentiality, integrity, or availability
    

Events shall be assessed to determine whether they constitute incidents.

---

## Incident Identification & Reporting

- All personnel shall promptly report:
    
    - Suspected or confirmed security incidents
        
    - Unusual system behavior
        
    - Data loss or disclosure
        
- Reporting channels shall be clearly defined and communicated
    
- No disciplinary action shall result from good- faith reporting
    

---

## Incident Assessment & Classification

- Reported events shall be assessed to determine:
    
    - Severity
        
    - Impact
        
    - Urgency
        
- Incidents shall be classified (e.g. low / medium / high / critical)
    
- Classification shall guide response and escalation
    

---

## Incident Response

Incident response activities may include:

- Containment of the incident
    
- Eradication of the root cause
    
- Recovery of systems and data
    
- Communication with relevant stakeholders
    

Response actions shall be documented and coordinated.

---

## Roles & Responsibilities

### Incident Response Team / Responsible Roles

- Coordinate incident handling activities
    
- Ensure timely response and escalation
    

### IT / Operations

- Provide technical support for containment and recovery
    
- Preserve system integrity
    

### Information Security Function

- Lead incident management process
    
- Assess security impact
    
- Coordinate communication and reporting
    

### Management

- Provide decision- making support
    
- Approve major response actions
    

### Users

- Report incidents promptly
    
- Cooperate with investigations
    

---

## Communication & Escalation

- Incident communication paths shall be defined
    
- Escalation shall occur based on severity and impact
    
- External communication shall be controlled and authorized
    

---

## Evidence Collection & Preservation

- Evidence shall be collected where required for:
    
    - Investigation
        
    - Legal or regulatory purposes
        
- Evidence handling shall preserve integrity and chain of custody
    

---

## Incident Logging & Documentation

- Incidents shall be recorded, including:
    
    - Description
        
    - Timeline
        
    - Actions taken
        
    - Outcomes
        
- Records shall support audits and improvement activities
    

---

## Learning & Improvement

- Incidents shall be reviewed after resolution
    
- Lessons learned shall be identified and documented
    
- Improvements may include:
    
    - Control enhancements
        
    - Process updates
        
    - Training or awareness improvements
        

---

## Third- Party Incidents

- Suppliers shall be required to report relevant incidents
    
- Third- party incidents affecting the organization shall be handled under these controls
    
- Contractual obligations shall be enforced
    

---

## Compliance & Enforcement

Failure to report or properly manage incidents may result in:

- Increased impact or damage
    
- Regulatory or contractual consequences
    
- Disciplinary action
    

---

## Review & Maintenance

Incident management controls shall be reviewed periodically to ensure:

- Continued effectiveness
    
- Alignment with threat landscape
    
- Integration with monitoring, risk management, and business continuity
    

---

## Related Controls

- [[Logging and Monitoring Controls]]
    
- [[Risk Management Controls]]
    
- [[Business Continuity Controls]]
    
- [[Data Protection Controls]]
    
- [[Third- Party Supplier Security Controls]]
    
- [[Continual Improvement Controls]]

446.content:

METADATA:{"tags":["ISO27001","Controls"],"parent":"ISMS Index","created":"2026/02/03 16:12:33","modified":"2026/02/12 09:29:22","chunkId":"02 Knowledge/ISO/ISMS/Controls/Document and Record Controls.md#0","heading":"Document and Record Controls"}

NOTE BLOCK CONTENT:

Back to  [[Controls Index]]

# Document and Record Controls

## Purpose

The purpose of these controls is to ensure that documents and records required by the Information Security Management System (ISMS) are properly created, maintained, controlled, protected, and retained.

Effective document and record controls ensure the availability, integrity, traceability, and reliability of information supporting the ISMS.

---

## Scope

These controls apply to:

- All ISMS- related documents and records
    
- Policies, procedures, standards, guidelines, and templates
    
- Operational records, logs, evidence, and reports
    
- Documents and records in electronic or physical form
    

---

## Control References

- **ISO/IEC 27001:2022 - Clause 7.5.1** - General
    
- **ISO/IEC 27001:2022 - Clause 7.5.2** - Creating and updating
    
- **ISO/IEC 27001:2022 - Clause 7.5.3** - Control of documented information
    

(Standard: **ISO/IEC 27001**)

---

## Policy Statement

Documented information required by the ISMS shall be controlled to ensure that it is available, accurate, up to date, protected, and used appropriately.

Records shall be maintained as evidence of conformity to ISMS requirements and retained in accordance with defined retention requirements.

---

## Types of Documented Information

### Documents

Examples include:

- Policies and standards
    
- Procedures and work instructions
    
- Guidelines and templates
    
- Plans and frameworks
    

### Records

Examples include:

- Audit results
    
- Risk assessments
    
- Training records
    
- Incident reports
    
- Change records
    
- Management review outputs
    

---

## Document Creation & Updating

- Documents shall be:
    
    - Identified with a title and unique reference where appropriate
        
    - Version controlled
        
    - Approved prior to use
        
- Changes to documents shall be reviewed and approved
    
- Obsolete documents shall be clearly identified and removed from active use
    

---

## Document Control

The organization shall ensure that:

- Current versions of documents are available where needed
    
- Documents are protected against unauthorized modification or deletion
    
- Access to documents is restricted based on need- to- know
    
- Distribution of documents is controlled
    

---

## Record Control

Records shall be:

- Protected against loss, damage, or unauthorized alteration
    
- Stored in secure and approved locations
    
- Legible, retrievable, and traceable
    
- Retained in accordance with defined retention periods
    

Records shall not be modified once finalized, unless correction procedures are defined.

---

## Access & Protection

- Access to documents and records shall be restricted based on role and responsibility
    
- Sensitive documents and records shall be protected using appropriate technical and organizational controls
    
- Backup and recovery measures shall apply to critical documented information
    

---

## Retention & Disposal

- Retention periods shall be defined for documents and records
    
- Documents and records shall not be retained longer than necessary
    
- Secure disposal methods shall be used when retention periods expire
    

---

## External Documents

- External documents relevant to the ISMS shall be identified and controlled
    
- Changes to external documents shall be monitored where applicable
    
- Use of outdated external documents shall be prevented
    

---

## Roles & Responsibilities

### Document Owners

- Ensure documents are accurate, approved, and up to date
    
- Review documents periodically
    

### Users

- Use only approved and current documents
    
- Protect documents and records under their control
    

### Information Security Function

- Define document and record control requirements
    
- Monitor compliance
    
- Support audits and continual improvement
    

---

## Monitoring & Compliance

- Compliance with document and record controls shall be monitored
    
- Deviations shall be addressed through corrective actions
    
- Records shall support audit and certification activities
    

---

## Review & Maintenance

These controls shall be reviewed periodically to ensure:

- Continued effectiveness
    
- Alignment with ISMS and business needs
    
- Compliance with ISO/IEC 27001 requirements
    

---

447.title: Data Retention Controls
447.content:
NOTE TITLE: [[Data Retention Controls]]

METADATA:{"tags":["ISO27001","Controls"],"parent":"ISMS Index","created":"2026/02/03 16:12:33","modified":"2026/02/12 09:29:22","chunkId":"02 Knowledge/ISO/ISMS/Controls/Data Retention Controls.md#0","heading":"Data Retention Controls"}

NOTE BLOCK CONTENT:

Back to  [[Controls Index]]

# Data Retention Controls

## Purpose

The purpose of these controls is to ensure that data is retained only for as long as necessary to meet business, legal, regulatory, and contractual requirements, and is securely disposed of when no longer required.

Effective data retention controls reduce legal risk, limit exposure in case of incidents, and support data protection and privacy principles.

---

## Scope

These controls apply to:

- All data created, processed, stored, or managed by the organization
    
- Structured and unstructured data
    
- Personal, confidential, and business- critical information
    
- Data stored in on- premises, cloud, backup, and third- party systems
    

---

## Control References

- **ISO/IEC 27001:2022 - Annex A 5.34** - Privacy and protection of personally identifiable information
    
- **ISO/IEC 27001:2022 - Annex A 8 (multiple controls)** - Secure handling, storage, and disposal of data
    
- **ISO/IEC 27001:2022 - Clause 6** - Planning (risk- based approach)
    

(Standard: **ISO/IEC 27001**)

---

## Policy Statement

Data shall be retained only for defined and approved periods that are justified by business, legal, regulatory, or contractual requirements.

Once retention periods expire, data shall be securely deleted or destroyed in a manner appropriate to its classification and sensitivity.

---

## Data Retention Principles

The organization shall ensure that:

- Retention periods are clearly defined and documented
    
- Data is not retained longer than necessary
    
- Retention requirements are based on risk, legal, and business needs
    
- Retention and disposal processes are consistently applied
    
- Retention controls are auditable and enforceable
    

---

## Definition of Retention Periods

- Retention periods shall be defined for data categories, such as:
    
    - Operational data
        
    - Financial and accounting records
        
    - Personnel data
        
    - Customer or client data
        
    - Logs and monitoring data
        
    - Backup data
        
- Retention periods shall consider:
    
    - Legal and regulatory obligations
        
    - Contractual requirements
        
    - Business needs
        
    - Risk assessments
        

Retention requirements shall be reviewed periodically.

---

## Data Storage During Retention

- Data shall be stored securely throughout its retention period
    
- Protection measures shall align with data classification
    
- Access to retained data shall remain restricted and monitored
    
- Archived data shall be protected against unauthorized access or alteration
    

---

## Backup & Retention Alignment

- Backup retention periods shall be defined and documented
    
- Backup retention shall align with data retention requirements where feasible
    
- Special consideration shall be given to:
    
    - Long- term backups
        
    - Immutable or off- site backups
        

---

## Secure Disposal & Destruction

- Data shall be securely deleted or destroyed once retention periods expire
    
- Disposal methods shall prevent reconstruction or recovery of data
    
- Secure disposal methods may include:
    
    - Logical deletion
        
    - Cryptographic erasure
        
    - Physical destruction of media
        
- Disposal activities shall be documented where appropriate
    

---

## Legal Hold & Retention Exceptions

- Retention periods may be suspended due to:
    
    - Legal hold
        
    - Litigation
        
    - Investigations
        
- Exceptions shall be:
    
    - Formally approved
        
    - Documented
        
    - Reviewed periodically
        

---

## Roles & Responsibilities

### Data Owners

- Define and approve retention requirements for their data
    
- Ensure retention aligns with business and legal needs
    

### Users

- Handle and store data according to retention requirements
    
- Avoid unnecessary duplication or prolonged storage
    

### IT / Operations

- Implement technical retention and deletion mechanisms
    
- Ensure retention policies are enforced across systems
    

### Information Security Function

- Define data retention standards
    
- Monitor compliance
    
- Support audits and corrective actions
    

---

## Monitoring & Compliance

- Compliance with data retention controls shall be monitored
    
- Non- compliance shall be addressed through corrective actions
    
- Retention and disposal activities shall support audit and regulatory reviews
    

---

## Review & Maintenance

These controls shall be reviewed periodically to ensure:

- Continued compliance with legal and regulatory requirements
    
- Alignment with business needs and risks
    
- Effectiveness of retention and disposal mechanisms
    

---

## Related Controls

- [[Information Classification and Handling Controls]]
    
- [[Backup Controls]]
    
- [[Incident Management Controls]]
    
- [[Third- Party Supplier Security Controls]]

448.title: Data Protection Controls
448.content:
NOTE TITLE: [[Data Protection Controls]]

METADATA:{"tags":["ISO27001","Controls"],"parent":"ISMS Index","created":"2026/02/03 16:12:33","modified":"2026/02/12 09:29:22","chunkId":"02 Knowledge/ISO/ISMS/Controls/Data Protection Controls.md#0","heading":"Data Protection Controls"}

NOTE BLOCK CONTENT:

Back to  [[Controls Index]]

# Data Protection Controls

## Purpose

The purpose of these controls is to ensure that information and data are protected against unauthorized access, disclosure, alteration, loss, or destruction throughout their lifecycle, in accordance with business, legal, regulatory, and contractual requirements.

Data protection controls support the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of information and help prevent data breaches and misuse.

---

## Scope

These controls apply to:

- All data processed, stored, or transmitted by the organization
    
- Structured and unstructured data
    
- Personal, confidential, and business- critical information
    
- Data handled by employees, contractors, and third parties
    
- On- premises, cloud, and third- party environments
    

---

## Control References

- **ISO/IEC 27001:2022 - Annex A 5.34** - Privacy and protection of personally identifiable information
    
- **ISO/IEC 27001:2022 - Annex A 8 (multiple controls)** - Secure data handling, storage, transmission
    

(Standard: **ISO/IEC 27001**)

---

## Policy Statement

Data shall be protected throughout its lifecycle using appropriate organizational and technical controls based on its classification, sensitivity, and associated risks.

Data protection requirements shall be integrated into business processes, systems, and services from design through disposal.

---

## Data Protection Principles

The organization shall ensure that:

- Data is processed lawfully, fairly, and for defined purposes
    
- Data access is restricted based on need- to- know and least privilege
    
- Data accuracy and integrity are maintained
    
- Data is protected against unauthorized disclosure or loss
    
- Data protection measures are proportionate to risk
    

---

## Data Classification & Handling

- Data shall be classified according to defined classification levels
    
- Classification shall determine:
    
    - Storage requirements
        
    - Access controls
        
    - Encryption requirements
        
    - Retention and disposal rules
        
- Data handling procedures shall align with classification
    

---

## Data Access & Authorization

- Access to data shall be formally authorized
    
- Role- based access controls shall be used where feasible
    
- Privileged access to sensitive data shall be limited and monitored
    
- Access rights shall be reviewed periodically
    

---

## Data Storage & Retention

- Data shall be stored in approved locations and systems
    
- Storage mechanisms shall protect against:
    
    - Unauthorized access
        
    - Accidental loss
        
    - Corruption
        
- Data retention periods shall be defined and documented
    
- Data shall not be retained longer than necessary
    

---

## Data Transmission & Sharing

- Data transmitted over networks shall be protected against interception or alteration
    
- Secure communication mechanisms shall be used where required
    
- Data sharing with third parties shall be:
    
    - Authorized
        
    - Documented
        
    - Limited to agreed purposes
        

---

## Data Minimization & Purpose Limitation

- Only data necessary for business purposes shall be collected and processed
    
- Data shall not be reused for incompatible purposes without authorization
    
- Redundant or unnecessary data shall be removed where feasible
    

---

## Data Integrity & Accuracy

- Measures shall be implemented to ensure data accuracy and integrity
    
- Unauthorized modification of data shall be prevented or detected
    
- Integrity controls shall be proportionate to data criticality
    

---

## Data Disposal & Destruction

- Data shall be securely deleted or destroyed when no longer required
    
- Disposal methods shall prevent reconstruction or recovery
    
- Disposal activities shall align with classification and retention requirements
    

---

## Roles & Responsibilities

### Data Owners

- Define data protection requirements
    
- Ensure appropriate classification and handling
    
- Approve access and sharing
    

### Users

- Handle data in accordance with policies and procedures
    
- Protect data against unauthorized disclosure
    
- Report suspected data breaches immediately
    

### IT / Operations

- Implement technical data protection controls
    
- Ensure secure storage, backup, and transmission
    

### Information Security Function

- Define data protection requirements
    
- Monitor compliance
    
- Support incident response and improvement activities
    

---

## Third- Party & Cloud Considerations

- Data protection requirements shall be addressed when engaging third parties
    
- Responsibilities for data protection shall be clearly defined
    
- Third- party data protection measures shall be assessed periodically
    

---

## Monitoring & Compliance

- Data protection controls shall be monitored for effectiveness
    
- Data protection incidents shall be handled through incident management processes
    
- Non- compliance shall be addressed through corrective actions
    

---

## Review & Maintenance

These controls shall be reviewed periodically to ensure:

- Alignment with business needs and risks
    
- Compliance with legal and regulatory requirements
    
- Continued effectiveness of protection measures
    

---

449.content:
NOTE TITLE: [[Cryptographic Key Management Controls]]

METADATA:{"tags":["ISO27001","Controls"],"parent":"ISMS Index","created":"2026/02/03 16:12:32","modified":"2026/02/12 09:29:22","chunkId":"02 Knowledge/ISO/ISMS/Controls/Cryptographic Key Management Controls.md#0","heading":"Cryptographic Key Management Controls"}

Back to  [[Controls Index]]

# Cryptographic Key Management Controls

## Purpose

The purpose of these controls is to ensure that cryptographic keys are securely managed throughout their entire lifecycle to prevent unauthorized disclosure, misuse, loss, or compromise.

Effective cryptographic key management is essential to maintaining the confidentiality, integrity, authenticity, and availability of encrypted information.

---

## Scope

These controls apply to:

- All cryptographic keys used to protect organizational information
    
- Encryption keys, signing keys, authentication keys, and certificates
    
- Key material used in systems, applications, networks, and backups
    
- On- premises, cloud, and third- party environments
    

---

## Control Reference

- **ISO/IEC 27001:2022 - Annex A 8.25** - Key management
    

(Standard: **ISO/IEC 27001**)

---

## Policy Statement

Cryptographic keys shall be securely generated, stored, distributed, used, rotated, revoked, and destroyed in accordance with defined key management requirements.

Access to cryptographic keys shall be restricted to authorized entities and aligned with the principle of least privilege.

---

## Key Management Principles

The organization shall ensure that:

- Cryptographic keys are protected against unauthorized access and disclosure
    
- Key management responsibilities are clearly defined
    
- Keys are used only for their intended purpose
    
- Key lifetimes are limited and controlled
    
- Compromised or obsolete keys are promptly revoked and replaced
    

---

## Key Lifecycle Management

Cryptographic keys shall be managed throughout the following lifecycle stages:

### Key Generation

- Keys shall be generated using approved cryptographic methods
    
- Key strength and parameters shall meet defined security standards
    
- Key generation shall occur in secure environments
    

---

### Key Storage & Protection

- Keys shall be stored securely using appropriate technical controls
    
- Access to stored keys shall be restricted and logged
    
- Keys shall be protected against:
    
    - Unauthorized access
        
    - Modification
        
    - Loss or destruction
        

---

### Key Distribution

- Key distribution shall be performed securely and in a controlled manner
    
- Keys shall only be distributed to authorized users, systems, or services
    
- Secure channels shall be used for key exchange
    

---

### Key Usage

- Keys shall be used only for approved cryptographic purposes
    
- Separation shall be maintained between different key types (e.g. encryption vs signing)
    
- Keys shall not be reused beyond their intended scope
    

---

### Key Rotation & Renewal

- Cryptographic keys shall be rotated based on:
    
    - Defined validity periods
        
    - Risk assessment
        
    - Cryptographic best practices
        
- Automated rotation mechanisms shall be used where feasible
    

---

### Key Revocation & Compromise Handling

- Keys shall be revoked immediately if:
    
    - Compromise is suspected or confirmed
        
    - Keys are no longer required
        
    - Cryptographic standards change
        
- Compromised keys shall be replaced without undue delay
    
- Key compromise events shall be handled as security incidents
    

---

### Key Destruction

- Keys shall be securely destroyed when no longer required
    
- Destruction methods shall prevent recovery of key material
    
- Key destruction shall be documented where appropriate
    

---

## Access Control & Segregation of Duties

- Access to cryptographic keys shall be restricted to authorized roles
    
- Segregation of duties shall be applied where feasible to prevent misuse
    
- Privileged access to key management systems shall be monitored
    

---

## Roles & Responsibilities

### System & Data Owners

- Define cryptographic key requirements
    
- Ensure keys align with information classification and risk
    

### IT / Operations

- Implement and maintain key management mechanisms
    
- Ensure secure storage, rotation, and revocation of keys
    

### Information Security Function

- Define key management standards and policies
    
- Approve key management practices
    
- Monitor compliance and investigate key- related incidents
    

---

## Third- Party & Cloud Considerations

- Key ownership and management responsibilities shall be clearly defined
    
- Where external services are used:
    
    - Key custody models shall be documented
        
    - Shared responsibility models shall be understood
        
- Third- party key handling practices shall be assessed
    

---

## Monitoring & Compliance

- Key management activities shall be logged where appropriate
    
- Logs shall support auditing and incident investigation
    
- Exceptions to key management requirements shall be documented and approved
    

---

## Review & Maintenance

These controls shall be reviewed periodically to ensure:

- Continued effectiveness of key management practices
    
- Alignment with cryptographic standards and threat landscape
    
- Compliance with legal, regulatory, and contractual obligations
    

---

## Related Controls

-[[Cryptographic Control and Encryption Controls]]
    
- [[Access Control Controls]]
    
- [[Incident Management Controls]]
    
-[[Logging and Monitoring Controls]]

METADATA:{"tags":["ISO27001","Controls"],"parent":"ISMS Index","created":"2026/02/03 16:12:32","modified":"2026/02/12 09:29:22","chunkId":"02 Knowledge/ISO/ISMS/Controls/Cryptographic Control and Encryption Controls.md#0","heading":"Cryptographic & Encryption Controls"}

NOTE BLOCK CONTENT:

Back to  [[Controls Index]]

# Cryptographic & Encryption Controls

## Purpose

The purpose of these controls is to ensure that cryptographic measures are used appropriately and effectively to protect the confidentiality, integrity, authenticity, and availability of information.

Cryptographic and encryption controls reduce the risk of unauthorized disclosure, tampering, and compromise of sensitive information.

---

## Scope

These controls apply to:

- All information assets requiring cryptographic protection
    
- All systems, applications, networks, and services processing protected information
    
- Cryptographic keys, certificates, and authentication secrets
    
- On- premises, cloud, and third- party environments
    

---

## Control References

- **ISO/IEC 27001:2022 - Annex A 8.24** - Use of cryptography
    
- **ISO/IEC 27001:2022 - Annex A 8.25** - Key management
    

(Standard: **ISO/IEC 27001**)

---

## Policy Statement

Cryptographic controls shall be implemented to protect information in accordance with business requirements, risk assessments, and information classification.

Cryptographic keys and related materials shall be securely generated, stored, distributed, used, rotated, and revoked throughout their lifecycle.

---

## Cryptographic Principles

The organization shall ensure that:

- Cryptographic controls are selected based on risk and data sensitivity
    
- Industry- accepted algorithms and protocols are used
    
- Cryptographic implementations are consistent and centrally governed
    
- Weak, deprecated, or broken cryptographic mechanisms are avoided
    

---

## Use of Encryption

Encryption shall be applied where appropriate to protect information:

### Data at Rest

- Sensitive information stored on systems, databases, backups, or removable media shall be encrypted where required
    
- Full- disk, file- level, or database encryption may be used depending on risk and architecture
    

### Data in Transit

- Sensitive information transmitted over networks shall be protected using secure communication protocols
    
- Encryption shall be used to protect data crossing untrusted or public networks
    

### Data in Use (where applicable)

- Additional protections may be applied for highly sensitive data processed in memory or shared environments
    

---

## Cryptographic Standards & Algorithms

- Approved cryptographic algorithms, key lengths, and protocols shall be defined and maintained
    
- Cryptographic standards shall be reviewed periodically to address emerging threats and deprecations
    
- Custom or proprietary cryptographic algorithms are prohibited unless formally approved
    

---

## Key Management

Cryptographic keys shall be managed throughout their lifecycle, including:

- Secure key generation
    
- Secure key storage and protection
    
- Controlled key distribution
    
- Defined key usage purposes
    
- Key rotation and renewal
    
- Key revocation and destruction
    

Key management practices shall prevent unauthorized access, loss, or misuse of keys.

---

## Protection of Cryptographic Material

- Cryptographic keys and secrets shall be protected against disclosure, modification, and loss
    
- Access to keys shall be restricted based on least privilege
    
- Where appropriate, hardware- based protections or managed key services shall be used
    

---

## Roles & Responsibilities

### System & Data Owners

- Determine cryptographic protection requirements
    
- Ensure encryption aligns with classification and risk
    

### IT / Operations

- Implement approved cryptographic solutions
    
- Maintain encryption configurations and key management systems
    

### Information Security Function

- Define cryptographic standards and requirements
    
- Approve cryptographic mechanisms
    
- Monitor compliance and review cryptographic risks
    

---

## Third- Party & Cloud Considerations

- Cryptographic requirements shall be considered when using third- party services
    
- Responsibilities for encryption and key management shall be clearly defined
    
- Encryption controls provided by external services shall be assessed for suitability
    

---

## Monitoring & Compliance

- Cryptographic implementations shall be monitored for compliance with standards
    
- Exceptions shall be documented, approved, and reviewed
    
- Failures or weaknesses in cryptographic controls shall be treated as security incidents where applicable
    

---

## Review & Maintenance

These controls shall be reviewed periodically to ensure:

- Continued effectiveness of cryptographic protections
    
- Alignment with evolving threats and best practices
    
- Compliance with legal, regulatory, and contractual requirements
    

---

## Related Controls

- [[Information Classification and Handling Controls]]
    
- [[Access Control Controls]]
    
- [[Backup Controls]]
    
- [[Logging and Monitoring Controls]]

## Info:

### Organisational Controls

Number of controls: 37
Control numbers: ISO 27001 Annex A 5.1 to 5.37
Organisational controls encompass regulations and measures which dictate an organisation’s comprehensive attitude towards data protection over a broad range of matters. These controls include policies, rules, processes, procedures, organisational structures and more.

### People Controls

Number of controls: 8
Control numbers: ISO 27001 Annex A 6.1 to 6.8
People controls enable businesses to regulate the human component of their information security program, by defining the manner in which personnel interact with data and each other. These controls cover secure human resources management, personnel security, and awareness and training.

### Physical 

Number of controls: 14
Control numbers: ISO 27001 Annex A 7.1 to 7.13
Physical safeguards are measures employed to ensure the security of tangible assets. These may include entry systems, guest access protocols, asset disposal processes, storage medium protocols, and clear desk policies. Such safeguards are essential for the preservation of confidential information.

### Technological Controls

Number of controls: 34
Control numbers: ISO 27001 Annex A 8.1 to 8.34
Technological restraints dictate the cybernetic/digital regulations and proceedings that corporations should adopt in order to execute a protected, compliant IT infrastructure, from authentication techniques to settings, BUDR strategies and information logging.
