452.title: Continual Improvement Controls
452.content:
NOTE TITLE: [[Continual Improvement Controls]]

METADATA:{"tags":["ISO27001","Controls"],"parent":"ISMS Index","created":"2026/02/03 16:12:32","modified":"2026/02/12 09:29:22","chunkId":"02 Knowledge/ISO/ISMS/Controls/Continual Improvement Controls.md#0","heading":"Continual Improvement Controls"}

NOTE BLOCK CONTENT:

Back to  [[Controls Index]]

# Continual Improvement Controls

## Purpose

The purpose of these controls is to ensure that the Information Security Management System (ISMS) is continually improved to maintain its effectiveness, address weaknesses, and adapt to changes in risks, technology, business objectives, and regulatory requirements.

Continual improvement ensures that information security remains relevant, effective, and aligned with organizational goals.

---

## Scope

These controls apply to:

- The entire Information Security Management System (ISMS)
    
- All information security policies, controls, and procedures
    
- All organizational units and processes within ISMS scope
    
- Internal and external factors affecting information security
    

---

## Control Reference

- **ISO/IEC 27001:2022 - Clause 10** - Improvement
    

(Standard: **ISO/IEC 27001**)

---

## Policy Statement

The organization shall continually improve the suitability, adequacy, and effectiveness of the ISMS through systematic identification, evaluation, and implementation of improvements.

Opportunities for improvement shall be identified through monitoring, measurement, audits, reviews, incidents, and feedback.

---

## Improvement Principles

Continual improvement shall be based on:

- Risk- based thinking
    
- Evidence and measurable outcomes
    
- Lessons learned from incidents and nonconformities
    
- Alignment with business objectives and strategy
    

---

## Identification of Improvement Opportunities

Opportunities for improvement may arise from:

- Internal audits
    
- Management reviews
    
- Risk assessments and risk treatment reviews
    
- Security incidents and near- misses
    
- Nonconformities and corrective actions
    
- Changes in legal, regulatory, or contractual requirements
    
- Feedback from stakeholders
    

---

## Nonconformities & Corrective Actions

- Nonconformities shall be identified, recorded, and assessed
    
- The organization shall:
    
    - Determine the root cause
        
    - Evaluate the need for corrective action
        
    - Implement actions to prevent recurrence
        
- Corrective actions shall be proportionate to the impact and risk
    

Evidence of corrective actions shall be retained.

---

## Monitoring & Measurement

- The effectiveness of controls and processes shall be monitored
    
- Key performance indicators (KPIs) and metrics may be used to:
    
    - Measure ISMS performance
        
    - Track trends over time
        
- Results shall be reviewed and used to drive improvements
    

---

## Management Review & Improvement

- Management shall regularly review the ISMS to:
    
    - Assess performance and effectiveness
        
    - Review audit results and incidents
        
    - Identify improvement opportunities
        
- Outputs from management reviews shall include:
    
    - Improvement actions
        
    - Resource needs
        
    - Strategic decisions
        

---

## Change & Improvement Integration

- Improvements shall be integrated into:
    
    - Policies and procedures
        
    - Technical and organizational controls
        
    - Awareness and training activities
        
- Improvements shall be implemented in a controlled and documented manner
    

---

## Documentation & Records

- Records of improvement activities shall be maintained
    
- Documentation shall demonstrate:
    
    - Identification of issues
        
    - Actions taken
        
    - Effectiveness of improvements
        

---

## Roles & Responsibilities

### Management

- Promote a culture of continual improvement
    
- Provide resources for improvement initiatives
    

### Information Security Function

- Coordinate continual improvement activities
    
- Track nonconformities, corrective actions, and improvements
    
- Report on ISMS effectiveness
    

### All Personnel

- Contribute to improvement by reporting issues and suggestions
    
- Comply with updated controls and procedures
    

---

## Compliance & Effectiveness

Failure to maintain continual improvement may result in:

- Degraded ISMS effectiveness
    
- Increased security risk
    
- Audit findings or certification issues
    

---

## Review & Maintenance

Continual improvement controls shall be reviewed periodically to ensure:

- Alignment with organizational objectives
    
- Ongoing effectiveness of the ISMS
    
- Incorporation of lessons learned and best practices
    

---

## Related Controls & Clauses

- [[Risk Management Controls]]
    
- [[Incident Management Controls]]
    
- [[Change Management Controls]]

### Note 😄

This page is your **“escape hatch” control** — if something isn’t perfect yet, auditors accept it _as long as you can show it’s being improved in a structured way_. This is where maturity lives.

# Clear Desk and Clear Screen Controls

## Purpose

The purpose of these controls is to reduce the risk of unauthorized access, loss, or disclosure of information by ensuring that sensitive information and systems are protected when not actively in use.

Clear desk and clear screen practices help safeguard information in offices, shared workspaces, remote locations, and public environments.

---

## Scope

These controls apply to:

- All employees, contractors, and third parties
    
- All work locations, including offices, home offices, and remote or temporary workspaces
    
- All information assets, regardless of format
    
- All devices used to access organizational information
    

---

## Control Reference

- **ISO/IEC 27001:2022 - Annex A 7.7** - Clear desk and clear screen
    

(Standard: **ISO/IEC 27001**)

---

## Policy Statement

Workspaces and information systems shall be secured when unattended to prevent unauthorized access, disclosure, loss, or damage to information and associated assets.

Sensitive information shall not be left exposed in physical or digital form when not actively required.

---

## Clear Desk Requirements

Users shall:

- Remove sensitive documents from desks when not in use
    
- Store physical information assets in locked cabinets or drawers where required
    
- Secure removable media when not in use
    
- Dispose of confidential waste using approved secure disposal methods
    

Users shall **not**:

- Leave confidential or restricted information unattended on desks
    
- Store sensitive information in unsecured locations
    

---

## Clear Screen Requirements

Users shall:

- Lock their screens when leaving devices unattended
    
- Use automatic screen locking with a defined inactivity timeout
    
- Ensure screens are positioned to reduce the risk of shoulder surfing
    
- Log out of systems at the end of the workday or when no longer required
    

Users shall **not**:

- Leave systems logged in and unattended
    
- Share active sessions with others
    

---

## Shared & Public Workspaces

- Additional care shall be taken in shared, open, or public environments
    
- Sensitive conversations shall be avoided where they may be overheard
    
- Portable devices shall not be left unattended in public spaces
    

---

## Remote & Home Working

- Clear desk and clear screen practices apply equally to remote work locations
    
- Work devices and information shall be protected from access by unauthorized household members or visitors
    
- Printed sensitive information should be minimized and securely stored
    

---

## Responsibilities

### Users

- Apply clear desk and clear screen practices consistently
    
- Protect information and devices under their control
    
- Report loss, theft, or suspected exposure of information immediately
    

### Management

- Promote awareness and compliance with clear desk and clear screen practices
    
- Support appropriate physical security measures
    

### Information Security Function

- Define clear desk and clear screen requirements
    
- Support awareness and training
    
- Monitor compliance where appropriate
    

---

## Compliance & Enforcement

Failure to comply with clear desk and clear screen controls may result in:

- Increased risk of information disclosure
    
- Disciplinary action
    
- Contractual or legal consequences
    

---

## Review & Maintenance

These controls shall be reviewed periodically to ensure:

- Continued relevance to working practices
    
- Alignment with physical security and remote working arrangements
    
- Effectiveness based on incident trends or audit findings
    

---

METADATA:{"tags":["ISO27001","Controls"],"parent":"ISMS Index","created":"2026/02/03 16:12:32","modified":"2026/02/12 09:29:22","chunkId":"02 Knowledge/ISO/ISMS/Controls/Change Management Controls.md#0","heading":"Change Management Controls"}

Back to  [[Controls Index]]

# Change Management Controls

## Purpose

The purpose of these controls is to ensure that changes to information systems, infrastructure, applications, and configurations are managed in a controlled manner to reduce the risk of unintended disruption, security weaknesses, or non- compliance.

Effective change management helps maintain the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of information assets while enabling controlled improvement.

---

## Scope

These controls apply to:

- Changes to information systems, applications, and infrastructure
    
- Changes to configurations, security controls, and system parameters
    
- Changes to processes supporting information processing
    
- Changes implemented by internal staff or third parties
    

---

## Control Reference

- **ISO/IEC 27001:2022 - Annex A 8.32** - Change management
    

(Standard: **ISO/IEC 27001**)

---

## Policy Statement

All changes that may impact information security or service availability shall be formally assessed, authorized, tested, implemented, and documented prior to deployment.

Emergency changes shall be controlled and reviewed retrospectively.

---

## Change Management Principles

The organization shall ensure that:

- Changes are justified by a business or technical need
    
- Risks associated with changes are identified and assessed
    
- Security impacts are considered before implementation
    
- Changes are traceable from request to completion
    
- Responsibilities are clearly defined
    

---

## Change Classification

Changes may be categorized, for example, as:

- **Standard changes** - Low risk, pre- approved, routine changes
    
- **Normal changes** - Require assessment, approval, and testing
    
- **Emergency changes** - Urgent changes to resolve incidents or critical risks
    

The level of control applied shall be proportionate to the risk and impact of the change.

---

## Change Request & Approval

- Changes shall be formally requested and documented
    
- Each change shall include:
    
    - Description and rationale
        
    - Impact and risk assessment
        
    - Security considerations
        
    - Rollback or recovery plan
        
- Changes shall be approved by appropriate authority prior to implementation
    

---

## Testing & Validation

- Changes shall be tested prior to deployment, where feasible
    
- Testing shall verify:
    
    - Functional correctness
        
    - Security requirements
        
    - Compatibility with existing systems
        
- Test results shall be documented
    

---

## Change Implementation

- Approved changes shall be implemented according to plan
    
- Changes shall be scheduled to minimize business impact
    
- Implementation activities shall be logged where appropriate
    

---

## Emergency Changes

- Emergency changes may bypass standard approval steps where necessary
    
- Emergency changes shall be:
    
    - Authorized by designated personnel
        
    - Documented as soon as possible
        
    - Reviewed after implementation to assess risk and impact
        

---

## Documentation & Traceability

- Records of changes shall be retained, including:
    
    - Requests
        
    - Approvals
        
    - Testing results
        
    - Implementation details
        
- Changes shall be traceable for audit and investigation purposes
    

---

## Roles & Responsibilities

### Change Requestors

- Provide accurate and complete change information
    
- Assess potential impacts and risks
    

### Approvers

- Evaluate risks and benefits
    
- Ensure security considerations are addressed
    

### IT / Operations

- Implement and test approved changes
    
- Maintain change records
    

### Information Security Function

- Review security- relevant changes
    
- Monitor compliance with change management requirements
    

---

## Compliance & Enforcement

Failure to comply with change management controls may result in:

- Service disruption
    
- Introduction of security vulnerabilities
    
- Disciplinary or contractual consequences
    

---

## Review & Maintenance

These controls shall be reviewed periodically to ensure:

- Continued effectiveness
    
- Alignment with business and security requirements
    
- Integration with incident and problem management processes
    

---

## Related Controls

- [[Backup Controls]]
    
- [[Logging and Monitoring Controls]]
    
- [[Incident Management Controls]]
    
- [[Business Continuity Controls]]

NOTE TITLE: [[Business Continuity Controls]]

METADATA:{"tags":["ISO27001","Controls"],"parent":"ISMS Index","created":"2026/02/03 16:12:32","modified":"2026/02/12 09:29:22","chunkId":"02 Knowledge/ISO/ISMS/Controls/Business Continuity Controls.md#0","heading":"Business Continuity Controls"}

NOTE BLOCK CONTENT:

Back to  [[Controls Index]]

# Business Continuity Controls

## Purpose

The purpose of these controls is to ensure that information security is maintained during disruptive events and that information and communication technology (ICT) systems are adequately prepared to support the continuation and recovery of critical business processes.

Business continuity controls reduce the impact of incidents and ensure the timely restoration of essential services.

---

## Scope

These controls apply to:

- All critical business processes
    
- Information assets supporting those processes
    
- ICT systems, applications, networks, and infrastructure
    
- Personnel and third parties involved in business continuity and recovery activities
    

---

## Control References

- **ISO/IEC 27001:2022 - Annex A 5.29** - Information security during disruption
    
- **ISO/IEC 27001:2022 - Annex A 5.30** - ICT readiness for business continuity
    

(Standard: **ISO/IEC 27001**)

---

## Policy Statement

The organization shall establish, implement, and maintain business continuity arrangements to ensure that information security and critical ICT services are maintained or restored within acceptable timeframes following a disruptive event.

Business continuity planning shall be aligned with business objectives, risk assessments, and information security requirements.

---

## Business Impact Analysis (BIA)

- A Business Impact Analysis shall be performed to:
    
    - Identify critical business processes
        
    - Assess the impact of disruptions
        
    - Define recovery priorities
        
- Dependencies on information, systems, personnel, and third parties shall be identified
    
- BIA results shall be reviewed periodically and upon significant change
    

---

## Continuity & Recovery Objectives

- Recovery objectives shall be defined for critical processes and systems, including:
    
    - Recovery Time Objectives (RTO)
        
    - Recovery Point Objectives (RPO)
        
- Objectives shall be aligned with business requirements and risk tolerance
    

---

## Business Continuity Planning

- Business continuity plans (BCPs) shall be documented and maintained
    
- Plans shall address:
    
    - Disruption scenarios
        
    - Roles and responsibilities
        
    - Communication procedures
        
    - Manual or alternative processing where applicable
        
- Information security requirements shall be integrated into all continuity plans
    

---

## ICT Readiness for Business Continuity

- ICT systems supporting critical processes shall be designed for resilience
    
- Measures may include:
    
    - Redundancy
        
    - Failover mechanisms
        
    - Backup and restoration capabilities
        
    - Capacity planning
        
- Continuity measures shall be proportionate to system criticality
    

---

## Information Security During Disruption

- Security controls shall remain effective during disruptive events
    
- Temporary or emergency access shall be:
    
    - Authorized
        
    - Logged
        
    - Reviewed after the event
        
- Confidentiality, integrity, and availability requirements shall be maintained wherever possible
    

---

## Testing & Exercising

- Business continuity and recovery plans shall be tested at planned intervals
    
- Testing may include:
    
    - Tabletop exercises
        
    - Technical recovery tests
        
    - Simulation of disruption scenarios
        
- Test results shall be documented and used to improve plans
    

---

## Roles & Responsibilities

### Management

- Approve business continuity strategies
    
- Ensure adequate resources for continuity planning
    

### Process & System Owners

- Define continuity requirements for their areas
    
- Participate in testing and reviews
    

### IT / Operations

- Implement ICT continuity measures
    
- Execute recovery procedures during incidents
    

### Information Security Function

- Ensure alignment between business continuity and information security
    
- Review continuity controls for effectiveness
    

---

## Third- Party & Supply Chain Considerations

- Business continuity requirements shall be considered when engaging third parties
    
- Dependencies on external services shall be identified and documented
    
- Third- party continuity capabilities shall be assessed where relevant
    

---

## Compliance & Enforcement

Failure to maintain adequate business continuity controls may result in:

- Prolonged service disruption
    
- Increased security risk
    
- Regulatory or contractual consequences
    

---

## Review & Maintenance

These controls shall be reviewed periodically to ensure:

- Alignment with business objectives
    
- Continued effectiveness following organizational or technological changes
    
- Lessons learned from incidents and tests are incorporated
    

---

## Related Controls

- [[Backup Controls]]
    
- [[Incident Management Controls]]
    
- [[Asset Management Controls]]
    
- [[Third- Party Supplier Security Controls]]

METADATA:{"tags":["ISO27001","Controls"],"parent":"ISMS Index","created":"2026/02/03 16:12:32","modified":"2026/02/12 09:29:22","chunkId":"02 Knowledge/ISO/ISMS/Controls/Backup Controls.md#0","heading":"Backup Controls"}

Back to  [[Controls Index]]

# Backup Controls

## Purpose

The purpose of this control is to ensure that information and other associated assets can be restored in a timely and reliable manner following incidents such as data loss, corruption, system failure, or cyber events.

Effective backup controls support business continuity, disaster recovery, and the protection of information availability and integrity.

---

## Scope

This control applies to:

- All information assets requiring protection against loss or corruption
    
- All systems, applications, databases, and platforms processing organizational information
    
- Backup data, storage media, and backup infrastructure
    
- On- premises, cloud, and third- party hosted environments
    

---

## Control Reference

- **ISO/IEC 27001:2022 - Annex A 8.13** - Information backup
    

(Standard: **ISO/IEC 27001**)

---

## Policy Statement

Backup copies of information, software, and system configurations shall be created, protected, tested, and maintained in accordance with defined backup requirements to ensure availability and recoverability.

Backup measures shall be proportionate to the business criticality and classification of the information.

---

## Backup Requirements

- Backup requirements shall be defined based on:
    
    - Business impact
        
    - Information classification
        
    - Legal and regulatory obligations
        
- Backup frequency, retention, and recovery objectives shall be documented
    
- Critical systems and data shall have clearly defined:
    
    - Recovery Point Objectives (RPO)
        
    - Recovery Time Objectives (RTO)
        

---

## Backup Scope & Coverage

Backups may include, where applicable:

- Business data and databases
    
- Application data and configurations
    
- System configurations and infrastructure definitions
    
- Security- relevant information (where permitted)
    

---

## Backup Execution

- Backups shall be performed according to a documented schedule
    
- Backup processes shall be automated where feasible
    
- Backup success and failures shall be monitored and addressed
    
- Backup jobs shall be logged for audit and troubleshooting purposes
    

---

## Backup Storage & Protection

- Backup data shall be protected against:
    
    - Unauthorized access
        
    - Alteration
        
    - Loss or destruction
        
- Backups shall be stored:
    
    - In physically and logically secure locations
        
    - Separately from primary systems where appropriate
        
- Encryption shall be used where required by classification or risk assessment
    

---

## Off- Site & Resilient Backups

- Off- site or geographically separated backups shall be used where appropriate
    
- Backup designs should consider protection against:
    
    - Ransomware
        
    - Accidental deletion
        
    - Single points of failure
        

---

## Backup Retention & Disposal

- Backup retention periods shall be defined and documented
    
- Retention shall consider:
    
    - Business requirements
        
    - Legal and regulatory obligations
        
- Expired backups shall be securely deleted or destroyed
    

---

## Backup Restoration & Testing

- Backup restoration procedures shall be documented
    
- Backups shall be tested at planned intervals to verify:
    
    - Data integrity
        
    - Recoverability
        
- Test results shall be reviewed and issues addressed
    

---

## Roles & Responsibilities

### System & Data Owners

- Define backup and recovery requirements
    
- Ensure backup coverage aligns with business needs
    

### IT / Operations

- Implement and maintain backup solutions
    
- Monitor backup jobs and storage
    
- Perform restoration tests
    

### Information Security Function

- Define backup control requirements
    
- Ensure alignment with risk assessments and classification
    
- Review backup practices for compliance
    

---

## Compliance & Enforcement

Failure to comply with backup control requirements may result in:

- Increased risk of data loss
    
- Service disruption
    
- Disciplinary or contractual consequences
    

---

## Review & Maintenance

This control shall be reviewed periodically to ensure:

- Backup coverage remains adequate
    
- Retention periods remain appropriate
    
- Alignment with business continuity and disaster recovery requirements
    

---

- [[Access Control Controls]]

METADATA:{"tags":["ISO27001","Controls"],"parent":"ISMS Index","created":"2026/02/03 16:12:32","modified":"2026/02/12 09:29:22","chunkId":"02 Knowledge/ISO/ISMS/Controls/Asset Management Controls.md#0","heading":"Asset Management"}

Back to  [[Controls Index]]

# Asset Management

## Purpose

The purpose of this control is to ensure that information and other associated assets are identified, inventoried, owned, and appropriately protected throughout their lifecycle.

Effective asset management ensures that assets receive a level of protection commensurate with their value, sensitivity, and criticality to the organization.

---

## Scope

This control applies to:

- All information assets, regardless of format or medium
    
- All physical and logical assets supporting information processing
    
- Assets owned, leased, or managed by the organization
    
- Assets provided by or shared with third parties
    

---

## Control References

- **ISO/IEC 27001:2022 - Annex A 5.9** - Inventory of information and other associated assets
    
- **ISO/IEC 27001:2022 - Annex A 5.10** - Acceptable use of information and other associated assets
    
- **ISO/IEC 27001:2022 - Annex A 5.11** - Return of assets
    
- **ISO/IEC 27001:2022 - Annex A 5.12** - Classification of information
    
- **ISO/IEC 27001:2022 - Annex A 5.13** - Labelling of information
    

(Standard: **ISO/IEC 27001**)

---

## Policy Statement

Information and other associated assets shall be identified, documented, assigned an owner, and protected throughout their lifecycle in accordance with business, legal, regulatory, and security requirements.

Assets shall be used, handled, stored, transferred, and disposed of in a controlled and secure manner.

---

## Asset Identification & Inventory

- An inventory of information and associated assets shall be maintained
    
- Assets shall be uniquely identifiable where appropriate
    
- The inventory shall include, at minimum:
    
    - Asset name or identifier
        
    - Asset type (information, software, hardware, service, etc.)
        
    - Owner
        
    - Location or system
        
    - Classification
        

The asset inventory shall be reviewed and kept up to date.

---

## Asset Ownership

- Each asset shall have a designated owner
    
- Asset owners are responsible for:
    
    - Ensuring appropriate classification
        
    - Defining protection requirements
        
    - Authorizing access
        
    - Ensuring compliance with policies
        

Ownership shall be updated when responsibilities change.

---

## Acceptable Use of Assets

- Assets shall be used only for authorized business purposes
    
- Users shall comply with documented acceptable use requirements
    
- Misuse, unauthorized use, or negligent handling of assets is prohibited
    

(See related **Acceptable Use** control.)

---

## Information Classification

- Information shall be classified based on:
    
    - Confidentiality
        
    - Integrity
        
    - Availability
        
- Classification levels shall be defined and documented
    
- Classification shall determine handling, storage, transmission, and protection requirements
    

---

## Labelling & Handling

- Information assets shall be labelled where appropriate to reflect their classification
    
- Labelling may be physical, logical, or metadata- based
    
- Handling procedures shall align with classification requirements
    

---

## Asset Lifecycle Management

Assets shall be managed throughout their lifecycle, including:

- Acquisition
    
- Use and maintenance
    
- Transfer or sharing
    
- Archiving
    
- Secure disposal or destruction
    

Controls shall ensure assets are protected at each stage.

---

## Return of Assets

- All assets issued to users or third parties shall be returned upon:
    
    - Termination of employment
        
    - End of contract
        
    - Role change, where applicable
        

Returned assets shall be verified and processed according to defined procedures.

---

## Responsibilities

### Asset Owners

- Maintain accurate asset information
    
- Ensure assets are appropriately protected
    
- Approve access and usage
    

### Users

- Use assets responsibly and according to policy
    
- Protect assets against loss, damage, or unauthorized access
    
- Report loss, theft, or misuse immediately
    

### Management

- Support asset management processes
    
- Ensure responsibilities are clearly assigned
    

---

## Compliance & Enforcement

Non- compliance with asset management requirements may result in:

- Access restriction or removal
    
- Disciplinary action
    
- Contractual or legal consequences
    

---

## Review & Maintenance

This control shall be reviewed periodically to ensure:

- Asset inventories remain accurate
    
- Classification remains appropriate
    
- Alignment with business, legal, and regulatory requirements
    

---

## Related Controls

458.content:

METADATA:{"tags":["ISO27001","Controls"],"parent":"ISMS Index","created":"2026/02/03 16:12:32","modified":"2026/02/12 09:29:22","chunkId":"02 Knowledge/ISO/ISMS/Controls/Access Control Controls.md#0","heading":"Access Control"}

NOTE BLOCK CONTENT:

Back to  [[Controls Index]]

# Access Control

## Purpose

The purpose of this control is to ensure that access to information and other associated assets is restricted to authorized users, processes, and systems only, in accordance with business and security requirements.

Effective access control reduces the risk of unauthorized access, data breaches, and misuse of information assets.

---

## Scope

This control applies to:

- All users (employees, contractors, third parties)
    
- All information systems, applications, networks, and services
    
- All information assets, regardless of classification or format
    

---

## Control References

- **ISO/IEC 27001:2022 - Annex A 5.15** - Access control
    
- **ISO/IEC 27001:2022 - Annex A 5.16** - Identity management
    
- **ISO/IEC 27001:2022 - Annex A 5.17** - Authentication information
    
- **ISO/IEC 27001:2022 - Annex A 5.18** - Access rights
    

(Standard: **ISO/IEC 27001**)

---

## Policy Statement

Access to information and associated assets shall be granted based on business need, using the principles of **least privilege** and **need- to- know**. Access rights shall be formally authorized, documented, reviewed, and revoked when no longer required.

---

## Access Control Principles

The organization shall ensure that:

- Access is granted only to authorized identities
    
- Users are uniquely identifiable where required
    
- Privileged access is tightly controlled and monitored
    
- Access rights align with job roles and responsibilities
    
- Segregation of duties is enforced where feasible
    

---

## Identity Management

- Each user shall be assigned a unique identity
    
- Shared or generic accounts are prohibited unless explicitly approved and justified
    
- User identities shall be lifecycle- managed (creation, modification, deactivation)
    
- Identity records shall be kept accurate and up to date
    

Identity provisioning and deprovisioning shall follow documented procedures.

---

## Authentication

- Authentication mechanisms shall be appropriate to the sensitivity of the system or data
    
- Strong authentication methods (e.g. MFA) shall be used where required
    
- Authentication credentials shall be protected against disclosure and misuse
    

Users shall **not**:

- Share authentication credentials
    
- Reuse organizational credentials on external systems
    
- Circumvent authentication mechanisms
    

---

## Authorization & Access Rights

- Access rights shall be granted based on approved requests
    
- Role- based access control (RBAC) should be used where possible
    
- Privileged access shall be restricted to a limited number of authorized users
    
- Temporary or elevated access shall be time- bound and reviewed
    

---

## Review of Access Rights

- Access rights shall be reviewed at regular intervals
    
- Reviews shall also occur upon:
    
    - Role or responsibility changes
        
    - Employment termination
        
    - Contract expiration
        

Unauthorized or unnecessary access shall be promptly removed.

---

## Privileged Access Management

- Administrative and privileged accounts shall be strictly controlled
    
- Privileged activities shall be logged and monitored
    
- Use of privileged access shall be limited to authorized tasks only
    

---

## Access Control for Third Parties

- Third- party access shall be limited to contractual and business requirements
    
- Access shall be approved, documented, and time- bound
    
- Third- party access shall be revoked immediately when no longer required
    

---

## Responsibilities

### Users

- Use access rights responsibly and only for authorized purposes
    
- Protect authentication information
    
- Report suspected unauthorized access immediately
    

### Management

- Approve access based on business needs
    
- Support periodic access reviews
    

### Information Security Function

- Define access control rules and standards
    
- Monitor compliance and investigate violations
    

---

## Compliance & Enforcement

Failure to comply with access control requirements may result in:

- Access revocation
    
- Disciplinary action
    
- Contractual or legal consequences
    

---

## Review & Maintenance

This control shall be reviewed periodically to ensure alignment with:

- Organizational changes
    
- Technology changes
    
- Legal and regulatory requirements
    
- ISO/IEC 27001 updates
    

---

## Related Controls

-[[Acceptable Use Controls]]
    
- [[Information Classification and Handling Controls]]
    
- [[Logging and Monitoring Controls]]
    
- [[Incident Management Controls]]

459.title: Acceptable Use Controls
459.content:
NOTE TITLE: [[Acceptable Use Controls]]

METADATA:{"tags":["ISO27001","Controls"],"parent":"ISMS Index","created":"2026/02/03 16:12:32","modified":"2026/02/12 09:29:22","chunkId":"02 Knowledge/ISO/ISMS/Controls/Acceptable Use Controls.md#0","heading":"Acceptable Use of Information & Assets"}

NOTE BLOCK CONTENT:

Back to  [[Controls Index]]

---

# Acceptable Use of Information & Assets

## Purpose

The purpose of this control is to ensure that information and other associated assets are used in a responsible, secure, and compliant manner, in line with the organization’s information security objectives and the requirements of **ISO/IEC 27001 (2022)**.

Clear acceptable use rules reduce the risk of misuse, data leakage, security incidents, and legal or regulatory non- compliance.

---

## Scope

This control applies to:

- All employees, contractors, interns, and third parties with access to organizational assets
    
- All information assets, regardless of format (digital, physical, verbal)
    
- All systems, services, devices, and networks owned, leased, or managed by the organization
    

---

## Control Reference

- **ISO/IEC 27001:2022 - Annex A 5.10**  
    _Acceptable use of information and other associated assets_
    

---

## Policy Statement

Information and associated assets shall only be used for authorized business purposes and in accordance with defined acceptable use rules. Users are responsible for protecting the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of the assets entrusted to them.

Misuse, unauthorized use, or negligent handling of information assets is prohibited.

---

## Acceptable Use Rules

### General Principles

Users shall:

- Use information assets only for legitimate business purposes
    
- Comply with all applicable laws, regulations, contracts, and internal policies
    
- Protect assets against unauthorized access, disclosure, modification, or destruction
    
- Follow the principle of least privilege when accessing systems and data
    

---

### Information Assets

Users shall:

- Access, process, store, and transmit information only when authorized
    
- Handle information according to its classification (e.g. public, internal, confidential)
    
- Avoid copying, sharing, or exporting information unless explicitly permitted
    
- Ensure sensitive information is not exposed in public or insecure environments
    

Users shall **not**:

- Circumvent security controls
    
- Access information outside their role or authorization
    
- Share credentials or authentication mechanisms
    

---

### IT Systems & Devices

Users shall:

- Use organizational devices and systems in accordance with documented procedures
    
- Keep systems protected using approved security controls (e.g. passwords, MFA)
    
- Lock devices when unattended
    
- Report loss, theft, or suspected compromise immediately
    

Users shall **not**:

- Install unauthorized software or hardware
    
- Disable or bypass security mechanisms
    
- Use systems for illegal, unethical, or unauthorized activities
    

---

### Network & Internet Usage

Users shall:

- Use network and internet access responsibly and in support of business activities
    
- Be aware that network usage may be logged and monitored for security purposes
    

Users shall **not**:

- Access malicious, illegal, or inappropriate content
    
- Introduce malware or malicious code
    
- Use organizational networks to attack or probe external systems
    

---

### Third- Party & Remote Access

Users shall:

- Use remote access solutions approved by the organization
    
- Ensure third- party access is limited to agreed purposes and durations
    
- Protect organizational assets when working remotely or off- site
    

---

## Responsibilities

### Users

- Understand and comply with acceptable use requirements
    
- Protect assets under their control
    
- Promptly report security incidents or suspected misuse
    

### Management

- Ensure acceptable use rules are communicated and enforced
    
- Support awareness and training initiatives
    

### Information Security Function

- Define, maintain, and review acceptable use rules
    
- Monitor compliance and investigate violations
    

---

## Awareness & Acknowledgement

All users shall be informed of acceptable use requirements and may be required to formally acknowledge their understanding and acceptance.

---

## Compliance & Enforcement

Violation of acceptable use rules may result in:

- Access revocation
    
- Disciplinary action
    
- Contractual consequences
    
- Legal action, where applicable
    

---

## Review & Maintenance

This control shall be reviewed periodically and updated as required to reflect:

- Changes in business operations
    
- Changes in technology
    
- Updates to legal, regulatory, or ISO requirements
    

---

- [[Access Control Controls]]
    
- [[Incident Management Controls]]

460.content:

METADATA:{"tags":["iso27001","structure","clauses"],"parent":"ISO27001 - Index","created":"2026/02/10 12:55:23","modified":"2026/02/12 09:50:49","chunkId":"02 Knowledge/ISO/ISO27001/ISO27001 - Structure of the Standard.md#0","heading":"ISO/IEC 27001 – Structure of the Standard"}

NOTE BLOCK CONTENT:

Back to [[ISO27001 - Overview]]

# ISO/IEC 27001 – Structure of the Standard

ISO/IEC 27001 consists of:
- **Clauses 4–10** (mandatory requirements)
- **Annex A** (reference control set)

## Clauses Overview

| Clause | Topic |
|------|------|
| 4 | Context of the organization |
| 5 | Leadership |
| 6 | Planning |
| 7 | Support |
| 8 | Operation |
| 9 | Performance evaluation |
| 10 | Improvement |

Clauses 4–10 define **what must exist** in the ISMS.

## Annex A
Annex A provides:
- A catalogue of information security controls
- Used as a **reference**, not a checklist

Our application of Annex A is documented in:
- [[Statement of Applicability]]
- [[Controls]]

461.title: ISO27001 - Risk Management Explained

# Risk Management Explained

ISO 27001 requires organizations to identify, assess and treat information security risks.

## Risk Flow
1. Identify assets
2. Identify threats and vulnerabilities
3. Assess likelihood and impact
4. Determine risk level
5. Select treatment options
6. Apply controls
7. Accept residual risk

## Risk Treatment Options
- Mitigate
- Avoid
- Transfer
- Accept

## Implementation
- Risks are recorded in [[Risk Register]]
- Controls selected are justified in [[Statement of Applicability]]

# ISO/IEC 27001 – Overview

ISO/IEC 27001 is an international standard that defines the requirements for an Information Security Management System (ISMS).

Its goal is to help organizations:
- Protect confidentiality, integrity and availability of information
- Manage information security risks systematically
- Demonstrate security governance to stakeholders

ISO 27001 is **risk-based**, not checklist-based.

## What ISO 27001 Is
- A **management system standard**
- Technology-agnostic
- Applicable to organizations of any size

## What ISO 27001 Is Not
- Not a technical hardening guide
- Not a fixed list of mandatory controls
- Not a one-time project

## Key Principle
> Security controls exist to treat *identified risks*, not to satisfy auditors.

## Relation to Our ISMS
- Our ISMS is documented under [[ISMS]]
- Controls are defined under [[Controls]]
- Risks are tracked in [[Risk Register]]

METADATA:{"tags":["iso27001","terminology","definitions"],"aliases":["ISO 27001 Glossary"],"parent":"ISO27001 Index","created":"2026/02/10 13:03:35","modified":"2026/02/12 09:51:04","chunkId":"02 Knowledge/ISO/ISO27001/ISO 27001 - Terminology.md#0","heading":"ISO/IEC 27001 – Terminology"}

# ISO/IEC 27001 – Terminology

ISO 27001 relies on precise terminology. Misunderstanding definitions is a common source of audit findings.

This note documents the most important terms **as used within our ISMS**.

## Key Terms

### Asset
Anything that has value to the organization.
Examples: information, systems, people, reputation.

### Threat
A potential cause of an unwanted incident.
Examples: malware, human error, fire, unauthorized access.

### Vulnerability
A weakness that can be exploited by a threat.
Examples: unpatched systems, lack of training, weak procedures.

### Risk
The combination of the likelihood of an event and its impact.

Risk = Threat × Vulnerability × Impact


### Risk Owner
Person responsible for managing a specific risk.

### Risk Treatment
The process of modifying risk.
Options:
- Mitigate
- Avoid
- Transfer
- Accept

### Control
A measure that modifies risk.
Controls can be:
- Preventive
- Detective
- Corrective

Controls are documented under [[Controls]].

### Statement of Applicability (SoA)
A document that:
- Lists selected Annex A controls
- Justifies inclusions and exclusions
- Shows implementation status

See [[Statement of Applicability]].

### Residual Risk
Risk remaining after controls have been applied.

### ISMS
Information Security Management System — the overall governance framework.

---

Clear terminology ensures consistent interpretation across:
- Risk assessments
- Policies
- Audits
- Management reviews

# Continuous Improvement

ISO 27001 requires continual improvement of the ISMS.

Security is not static — threats, technology and business contexts change continuously.

## PDCA Cycle

ISO 27001 is built on the **Plan–Do–Check–Act (PDCA)** model.

### Plan
- Define scope
- Perform risk assessment
- Define controls
- Set objectives

References:
- [[ISMS Scope]]
- [[Risk Register]]
- [[Statement of Applicability]]

### Do
- Implement controls
- Train personnel
- Operate processes

References:
- [[Controls]]
- [[Information Security Awareness and Training Controls]]

### Check
- Monitor controls
- Review incidents
- Perform audits
- Measure performance

References:
- [[Logging and Monitoring Controls]]
- [[Incident Management]]
- [[Internal Audit]]

### Act
- Address nonconformities
- Improve controls
- Update risk assessments

References:
- [[Corrective Actions]]
- [[Management Review]]

## Evidence of Improvement

Auditors typically expect:
- Updated risk assessments
- Revised policies
- Control enhancements
- Lessons learned from incidents

## Our Improvement Mechanisms
- Management reviews
- Incident post-mortems
- Audit findings
- Risk reassessments

Continuous improvement demonstrates **governance maturity**, not just compliance.

METADATA:{"tags":["obsidian"],"domain":"obsidian","subcategory":"meta","aliases":["Structure"],"created":"2026/02/04 09:08:28","modified":"2026/02/12 09:29:22","chunkId":"00 Meta/Obsidian/Vault Structure.md#0","heading":"Canonical Folder Layout"}

NOTE BLOCK CONTENT:

Back to  [[Obsidian Index]]

> _Folders are scaffolding, not meaning._

## Canonical Folder Layout

```text
00 Meta/        → Vault rules, systems, templates
01 Inbox/       → Fast capture, zero friction
02 Knowledge/   → Atomic, evergreen ideas
03 Projects/    → Time-bound work with outcomes
04 Areas/       → Ongoing responsibilities
05 Resources/   → External references
99 Archive/     → Inactive but kept notes
```

---

## Folder Rules

### 00 Meta

- Rules about the vault itself
    
- Templates, workflows, system notes
    
- Never archived
    

---

### 01 Inbox

- Temporary
    
- Unstructured
    
- Must be reviewed regularly
    

Inbox is **not failure** — it’s a buffer.

---

### 02 Knowledge

- One idea per note
    
- No deadlines
    
- Heavy linking
    
- Long-term value
    

---

### 03 Projects

- Has a goal
    
- Has tasks
    
- Has an end
    

When done → Archive.

---

### 04 Areas

- No end date
    
- Ongoing responsibility
    
- Light task tracking
    

---

### 05 Resources

- External material
    
- Read-only mindset
    
- Not original thinking
    

---

### 99 Archive

- Closed projects
    
- Outdated notes
    
- Still searchable
    

---

## Structural Rules

- No deep nesting unless unavoidable
    
- Do not encode meaning in folder depth
    
- If unsure where something goes → Inbox

## Knowledge Note

**Purpose:** Capture and evolve ideas.

`type: knowledge status: evergreen`

**Rules**

- One core idea
    
- Links to related concepts
    
- No tasks unless inherent to the concept
    

---

## Project Note

**Purpose:** Track work with an outcome.

`type: project status: active`

**Must include**

- Clear goal
    
- Tasks
    
- Links to relevant knowledge
    

---

## Area Note

**Purpose:** Represent ongoing responsibilities.

`type: area`

Examples:

- Health
    
- Career
    
- Personal Development
    

---

## Inbox Note

**Purpose:** Temporary holding space.

`type: inbox`

Rules:

- No structure required
    
- Must be processed or deleted
    
- Not meant to live long-term
    

---

## Daily Note

**Purpose:** Time-based log.

`type: daily`

Rules:

- Logs, not essays
    
- Links encouraged
    
- Tasks allowed
    

---

## General Rules

- Do not invent new note types casually
    
- If you do invent one, document it here
    
- Metadata exists to support queries, not aesthetics

479.title: Obsidian Knowledge System
479.content:
NOTE TITLE: [[Obsidian Knowledge System]]

METADATA:{"tags":["obsidian"],"domain":"obsidian","subcategory":"meta","aliases":["Vault System"],"created":"2026/02/04 09:08:28","modified":"2026/02/12 09:29:22","chunkId":"00 Meta/Obsidian/Obsidian Knowledge System.md#0","heading":"Purpose"}

NOTE BLOCK CONTENT:

Back to  [[Obsidian Index]]

> _The operating system of this vault._

## Purpose

This document defines **how and why** this Obsidian vault is used.  
When unsure where something belongs, how to write a note, or whether something should exist at all — start here.

This document is **authoritative**.

---

## Core Principles

### 1. Notes are thinking tools

- Notes are not documents, archives, or blogs
    
- Notes exist to **clarify thinking**
    
- Imperfect notes are acceptable; unused notes are not
    

---

### 2. Atomic by default

- One note = one idea
    
- Notes must make sense when opened directly
    
- If a note feels like a chapter, split it
    

---

### 3. Links over hierarchy

- Folders are logistical, not semantic
    
- Meaning comes from links and context
    
- If something belongs in multiple places → link it
    

---

### 4. Capture first, organize later

- Inbox is allowed to be messy
    
- Organization happens during review, not capture
    
- Speed beats structure in the moment
    

---

## Golden Rules

- Every note should eventually link to _something_
    
- If you write the same thing twice, create a note for it
    
- If a process repeats, document it
    
- If future-me would ask “why?”, explain it now
    

---

## When Lost

Ask these questions **in order**:

1. Is this actionable? → Project / Task
    
2. Is this an idea worth keeping? → Knowledge
    
3. Is this ongoing responsibility? → Area
    
4. Is this raw / unclear? → Inbox
    

If still unclear → Inbox, review later.

# Acceptable Use of Information & Assets

## Purpose

The purpose of this control is to ensure that information and other associated assets are used in a responsible, secure, and compliant manner, in line with the organization’s information security objectives and the requirements of **ISO/IEC 27001 (2022)**.

Clear acceptable use rules reduce the risk of misuse, data leakage, security incidents, and legal or regulatory non- compliance.

---

## Scope

This control applies to:

- All employees, contractors, interns, and third parties with access to organizational assets
    
- All information assets, regardless of format (digital, physical, verbal)
    
- All systems, services, devices, and networks owned, leased, or managed by the organization
    

---

## Control Reference

- **ISO/IEC 27001:2022 - Annex A 5.10**  
    _Acceptable use of information and other associated assets_
    

---

## Policy Statement

Information and associated assets shall only be used for authorized business purposes and in accordance with defined acceptable use rules. Users are responsible for protecting the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of the assets entrusted to them.

Misuse, unauthorized use, or negligent handling of information assets is prohibited.

---

## Acceptable Use Rules

### General Principles

Users shall:

- Use information assets only for legitimate business purposes
    
- Comply with all applicable laws, regulations, contracts, and internal policies
    
- Protect assets against unauthorized access, disclosure, modification, or destruction
    
- Follow the principle of least privilege when accessing systems and data
    

---

### Information Assets

Users shall:

- Access, process, store, and transmit information only when authorized
    
- Handle information according to its classification (e.g. public, internal, confidential)
    
- Avoid copying, sharing, or exporting information unless explicitly permitted
    
- Ensure sensitive information is not exposed in public or insecure environments
    

Users shall **not**:

- Circumvent security controls
    
- Access information outside their role or authorization
    
- Share credentials or authentication mechanisms
    

---

### IT Systems & Devices

Users shall:

- Use organizational devices and systems in accordance with documented procedures
    
- Keep systems protected using approved security controls (e.g. passwords, MFA)
    
- Lock devices when unattended
    
- Report loss, theft, or suspected compromise immediately
    

Users shall **not**:

- Install unauthorized software or hardware
    
- Disable or bypass security mechanisms
    
- Use systems for illegal, unethical, or unauthorized activities
    

---

### Network & Internet Usage

Users shall:

- Use network and internet access responsibly and in support of business activities
    
- Be aware that network usage may be logged and monitored for security purposes
    

Users shall **not**:

- Access malicious, illegal, or inappropriate content
    
- Introduce malware or malicious code
    
- Use organizational networks to attack or probe external systems
    

---

### Third- Party & Remote Access

Users shall:

- Use remote access solutions approved by the organization
    
- Ensure third- party access is limited to agreed purposes and durations
    
- Protect organizational assets when working remotely or off- site
    

---

## Responsibilities

### Users

- Understand and comply with acceptable use requirements
    
- Protect assets under their control
    
- Promptly report security incidents or suspected misuse
    

### Management

- Ensure acceptable use rules are communicated and enforced
    
- Support awareness and training initiatives
    

### Information Security Function

- Define, maintain, and review acceptable use rules
    
- Monitor compliance and investigate violations
    

---

## Awareness & Acknowledgement

All users shall be informed of acceptable use requirements and may be required to formally acknowledge their understanding and acceptance.

---

## Compliance & Enforcement

Violation of acceptable use rules may result in:

- Access revocation
    
- Disciplinary action
    
- Contractual consequences
    
- Legal action, where applicable
    

---

## Review & Maintenance

This control shall be reviewed periodically and updated as required to reflect:

- Changes in business operations
    
- Changes in technology
    
- Updates to legal, regulatory, or ISO requirements
    

---

- [[Information Classification and Handling Controls]]
    
- [[Access Control Controls]]
    
- [[Incident Management Controls]]

# Access Control

## Purpose

The purpose of this control is to ensure that access to information and other associated assets is restricted to authorized users, processes, and systems only, in accordance with business and security requirements.

Effective access control reduces the risk of unauthorized access, data breaches, and misuse of information assets.

---

## Scope

This control applies to:

- All users (employees, contractors, third parties)
    
- All information systems, applications, networks, and services
    
- All information assets, regardless of classification or format
    

---

## Control References

- **ISO/IEC 27001:2022 - Annex A 5.15** - Access control
    
- **ISO/IEC 27001:2022 - Annex A 5.16** - Identity management
    
- **ISO/IEC 27001:2022 - Annex A 5.17** - Authentication information
    
- **ISO/IEC 27001:2022 - Annex A 5.18** - Access rights
    

(Standard: **ISO/IEC 27001**)

---

## Policy Statement

Access to information and associated assets shall be granted based on business need, using the principles of **least privilege** and **need- to- know**. Access rights shall be formally authorized, documented, reviewed, and revoked when no longer required.

---

## Access Control Principles

The organization shall ensure that:

- Access is granted only to authorized identities
    
- Users are uniquely identifiable where required
    
- Privileged access is tightly controlled and monitored
    
- Access rights align with job roles and responsibilities
    
- Segregation of duties is enforced where feasible
    

---

## Identity Management

- Each user shall be assigned a unique identity
    
- Shared or generic accounts are prohibited unless explicitly approved and justified
    
- User identities shall be lifecycle- managed (creation, modification, deactivation)
    
- Identity records shall be kept accurate and up to date
    

Identity provisioning and deprovisioning shall follow documented procedures.

---

## Authentication

- Authentication mechanisms shall be appropriate to the sensitivity of the system or data
    
- Strong authentication methods (e.g. MFA) shall be used where required
    
- Authentication credentials shall be protected against disclosure and misuse
    

Users shall **not**:

- Share authentication credentials
    
- Reuse organizational credentials on external systems
    
- Circumvent authentication mechanisms
    

---

## Authorization & Access Rights

- Access rights shall be granted based on approved requests
    
- Role- based access control (RBAC) should be used where possible
    
- Privileged access shall be restricted to a limited number of authorized users
    
- Temporary or elevated access shall be time- bound and reviewed
    

---

## Review of Access Rights

- Access rights shall be reviewed at regular intervals
    
- Reviews shall also occur upon:
    
    - Role or responsibility changes
        
    - Employment termination
        
    - Contract expiration
        

Unauthorized or unnecessary access shall be promptly removed.

---

## Privileged Access Management

- Administrative and privileged accounts shall be strictly controlled
    
- Privileged activities shall be logged and monitored
    
- Use of privileged access shall be limited to authorized tasks only
    

---

## Access Control for Third Parties

- Third- party access shall be limited to contractual and business requirements
    
- Access shall be approved, documented, and time- bound
    
- Third- party access shall be revoked immediately when no longer required
    

---

## Responsibilities

### Users

- Use access rights responsibly and only for authorized purposes
    
- Protect authentication information
    
- Report suspected unauthorized access immediately
    

### Management

- Approve access based on business needs
    
- Support periodic access reviews
    

### Information Security Function

- Define access control rules and standards
    
- Monitor compliance and investigate violations
    

---

## Compliance & Enforcement

Failure to comply with access control requirements may result in:

- Access revocation
    
- Disciplinary action
    
- Contractual or legal consequences
    

---

## Review & Maintenance

This control shall be reviewed periodically to ensure alignment with:

- Organizational changes
    
- Technology changes
    
- Legal and regulatory requirements
    
- ISO/IEC 27001 updates
    

---

## Related Controls

- [[Information Classification and Handling Controls]]
    
- [[Logging and Monitoring Controls]]

# Asset Management

## Purpose

The purpose of this control is to ensure that information and other associated assets are identified, inventoried, owned, and appropriately protected throughout their lifecycle.

Effective asset management ensures that assets receive a level of protection commensurate with their value, sensitivity, and criticality to the organization.

---

## Scope

This control applies to:

- All information assets, regardless of format or medium
    
- All physical and logical assets supporting information processing
    
- Assets owned, leased, or managed by the organization
    
- Assets provided by or shared with third parties
    

---

## Control References

- **ISO/IEC 27001:2022 - Annex A 5.9** - Inventory of information and other associated assets
    
- **ISO/IEC 27001:2022 - Annex A 5.10** - Acceptable use of information and other associated assets
    
- **ISO/IEC 27001:2022 - Annex A 5.11** - Return of assets
    
- **ISO/IEC 27001:2022 - Annex A 5.12** - Classification of information
    
- **ISO/IEC 27001:2022 - Annex A 5.13** - Labelling of information
    

(Standard: **ISO/IEC 27001**)

---

## Policy Statement

Information and other associated assets shall be identified, documented, assigned an owner, and protected throughout their lifecycle in accordance with business, legal, regulatory, and security requirements.

Assets shall be used, handled, stored, transferred, and disposed of in a controlled and secure manner.

---

## Asset Identification & Inventory

- An inventory of information and associated assets shall be maintained
    
- Assets shall be uniquely identifiable where appropriate
    
- The inventory shall include, at minimum:
    
    - Asset name or identifier
        
    - Asset type (information, software, hardware, service, etc.)
        
    - Owner
        
    - Location or system
        
    - Classification
        

The asset inventory shall be reviewed and kept up to date.

---

## Asset Ownership

- Each asset shall have a designated owner
    
- Asset owners are responsible for:
    
    - Ensuring appropriate classification
        
    - Defining protection requirements
        
    - Authorizing access
        
    - Ensuring compliance with policies
        

Ownership shall be updated when responsibilities change.

---

## Acceptable Use of Assets

- Assets shall be used only for authorized business purposes
    
- Users shall comply with documented acceptable use requirements
    
- Misuse, unauthorized use, or negligent handling of assets is prohibited
    

(See related **Acceptable Use** control.)

---

## Information Classification

- Information shall be classified based on:
    
    - Confidentiality
        
    - Integrity
        
    - Availability
        
- Classification levels shall be defined and documented
    
- Classification shall determine handling, storage, transmission, and protection requirements
    

---

## Labelling & Handling

- Information assets shall be labelled where appropriate to reflect their classification
    
- Labelling may be physical, logical, or metadata- based
    
- Handling procedures shall align with classification requirements
    

---

## Asset Lifecycle Management

Assets shall be managed throughout their lifecycle, including:

- Acquisition
    
- Use and maintenance
    
- Transfer or sharing
    
- Archiving
    
- Secure disposal or destruction
    

Controls shall ensure assets are protected at each stage.

---

## Return of Assets

- All assets issued to users or third parties shall be returned upon:
    
    - Termination of employment
        
    - End of contract
        
    - Role change, where applicable
        

Returned assets shall be verified and processed according to defined procedures.

---

## Responsibilities

### Asset Owners

- Maintain accurate asset information
    
- Ensure assets are appropriately protected
    
- Approve access and usage
    

### Users

- Use assets responsibly and according to policy
    
- Protect assets against loss, damage, or unauthorized access
    
- Report loss, theft, or misuse immediately
    

### Management

- Support asset management processes
    
- Ensure responsibilities are clearly assigned
    

---

## Compliance & Enforcement

Non- compliance with asset management requirements may result in:

- Access restriction or removal
    
- Disciplinary action
    
- Contractual or legal consequences
    

---

## Review & Maintenance

This control shall be reviewed periodically to ensure:

- Asset inventories remain accurate
    
- Classification remains appropriate
    
- Alignment with business, legal, and regulatory requirements
    

---

## Related Controls

- [[Acceptable Use Controls]]
    
- [[Access Control Controls]]
    
- [[Information Classification and Handling Controls]]
    
- [[Physical and Environmental Security Controls]]
    
- [[Incident Management Controls]]

# AWS Account Structure

## What this is
An AWS account is the **primary security and billing boundary** in AWS.

## Why it exists
To isolate workloads, control access, and separate billing.

## Core components
- **Root user**: Full control (should never be used day- to- day)
- **IAM users / roles**
- **Account ID** (12 digits)

## Multi- account strategy
Best practice:
- One account per environment (dev / test / prod)
- Centralized billing via AWS Organizations
- Shared services account (optional)

## AWS Organizations
- Group multiple accounts
- Apply **Service Control Policies (SCPs)**
- Centralize billing

## Common pitfalls
- Using the root user
- Running everything in one account
- No isolation between environments

## Terraform relevance
- Each account typically maps to a Terraform provider alias
- Cross- account access relies on IAM roles

# AWS Compute Decision Tree

Goal: choose the right compute option without overthinking it.

## Decision tree

1) **Is it event- driven or short tasks (seconds- minutes)?**
- Yes → **Lambda**
- No → go to 2

2) **Do you need to run containers?**
- Yes → go to 3
- No → go to 5

3) **Do you want to manage Kubernetes?**
- Yes → **EKS**
- No → go to 4

4) **Do you want AWS to manage the container orchestration layer?**
- Yes → **ECS** (often simplest)
- No / portability required → **EKS**

5) **Do you need full OS control (custom agents, legacy apps, special drivers)?**
- Yes → **EC2**
- No → go to 6

6) **Is it a web app/API that fits a managed platform model?**
- Yes → **Elastic Beanstalk** or **App Runner** (if you use it)
- No → **EC2** (default safe choice)

## Notes / heuristics
- If you’re unsure: **EC2** is the “least surprises” baseline.
- If you want lowest ops overhead for containers: **ECS** beats EKS for many teams.
- If you have spiky traffic and stateless compute: **Lambda** can be a cost and ops win.

## Pitfalls
- Choosing EKS for “future- proofing” without a Kubernetes need.
- Forcing Lambda into long- running or heavy CPU tasks.
- Running everything on EC2 because “that’s what we know” when containers would simplify releases.

## Related
- [[AWS IAM + CI-CD Authentication]]
- [[AWS VPC Architecture Patterns]]

# AWS Global Infrastructure

## What this is
AWS runs its services across a global network of **Regions**, each containing multiple isolated **Availability Zones (AZs)**, designed for high availability and fault tolerance.

## Why it exists
To allow workloads to:
- Survive data- center failures
- Be deployed close to users
- Meet regulatory and latency requirements

## Key concepts
- **Region**: A geographic area (e.g. `eu- west-1`)
- **Availability Zone (AZ)**: One or more isolated data centers within a region
- **Edge Locations**: Used for CloudFront and low- latency delivery

## Important behaviors
- AZs are isolated but connected with high- bandwidth links
- AZ names (`a`, `b`, `c`) are **account- specific**
- Not all services are available in all regions

## Common pitfalls
- Assuming `eu- west-1a` is the same AZ across accounts
- Designing “multi- AZ” systems but placing everything in one subnet
- Ignoring region availability when planning services

## Terraform relevance
- Regions are provider- scoped
- AZs often discovered dynamically via data sources

# AWS IAM + CI/CD Authentication

This note explains **how CI/CD systems authenticate to AWS**, and why roles + temporary credentials are the only sane option.

---

## The core problem
CI/CD systems need to:
- Authenticate non- interactively
- Access AWS securely
- Avoid long- lived secrets
- Work across accounts and environments

IAM solves this using **roles + temporary credentials**.

---

## The golden rule
> **CI/CD systems must never use IAM users with static access keys.**

If you see:
- `AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID` stored long- term
- Credentials committed to Git
- Shared keys across environments

That’s technical debt (and a security risk).

---

## The modern solution: AssumeRole

### High- level flow
1. CI/CD system authenticates **itself**
2. AWS issues **temporary credentials**
3. Pipeline uses those credentials
4. Credentials expire automatically

This is implemented using:
- IAM Roles
- STS
- Trust Policies

---

## Common CI/CD authentication patterns

### 1️⃣ GitHub Actions (OIDC - preferred)

#### How it works
- GitHub acts as an OIDC identity provider
- AWS trusts GitHub tokens
- No secrets stored

#### Components
- IAM OIDC Provider
- IAM Role with trust policy
- GitHub workflow assumes role

#### Benefits
- No long- lived secrets
- Per- repo and per- branch control
- Short- lived credentials

> This is the **best- practice** pattern today.

---

### 2️⃣ GitLab CI (AssumeRole with credentials)

#### Typical setup
- One bootstrap credential (limited)
- Pipeline assumes a deployment role
- Temporary credentials used for actions

#### Variants
- IAM User → AssumeRole (legacy)
- GitLab OIDC → AssumeRole (modern, preferred)

#### Risks
- Misconfigured trust policy
- Over- permissioned bootstrap credentials

---

### 3️⃣ Self- hosted CI (EC2 / Runner)

#### Pattern
- CI runner runs on EC2
- EC2 has an **instance profile**
- Instance assumes role automatically

#### Benefits
- No credentials in pipelines
- Transparent credential rotation

---

## Trust policies (where most failures occur)

### What a trust policy does
Defines **who is allowed to assume a role**.

Example trust relationships:
- `ec2.amazonaws.com`
- `sts.amazonaws.com`
- GitHub OIDC provider
- Another AWS account

If trust is wrong:
- AssumeRole fails
- Permissions don’t matter

---

## Permission policies (second most common failure)

Once the role is assumed:
- Permission policy defines allowed actions
- Missing permissions = runtime failure

Typical mistakes:
- Forgetting `sts:AssumeRole`
- Missing `iam:PassRole`
- Over- restrictive resource ARNs

---

## Multi- account CI/CD (real- world pattern)

### Typical setup
- Central CI/CD account
- One role per target account
- CI assumes environment- specific roles

Example:
- `ci- deploy- dev`
- `ci- deploy- prod`

### Benefits
- Strong isolation
- Blast radius control
- Clear audit trail

---

## Environment separation strategy

| Environment | AWS Account | IAM Role |
|------------|-----------|----------|
| Dev | Dev Account | ci- deploy- dev |
| Test | Test Account | ci- deploy- test |
| Prod | Prod Account | ci- deploy- prod |

Never reuse the same role across environments.

---

## Debugging IAM + CI/CD failures

### Step- by- step checklist
1. Does the pipeline authenticate at all?
2. Does AssumeRole succeed?
3. Is the trust policy correct?
4. Does the role have permissions?
5. Are SCPs blocking access?
6. Is the correct account targeted?

### Tools
- CloudTrail
- AWS CLI `sts get- caller- identity`
- Terraform plan output

---

## Terraform relevance

Terraform in CI/CD typically:
- Uses `assume_role`
- Targets multiple accounts
- Requires IAM bootstrapping

Common patterns:
- One provider per account
- Explicit role ARNs
- Separate state per environment

See also:
- [[Terraform AWS Provider]]
- [[Terraform IAM Modules]]
- [[AWS IAM Deep Dive]]

---

## Security best practices (non- negotiable)

- Use OIDC where possible
- Use short session durations
- Scope roles tightly
- Log all role assumptions
- Rotate and delete legacy keys

---

## When to revisit this note
- Pipeline authentication fails
- Moving from static keys to OIDC
- Introducing new environments
- Security audits

# AWS IAM + Terraform

This note documents **how IAM is actually used with Terraform**, including common patterns and failure modes.

---

## The core problem
Terraform needs AWS permissions to:
- Read existing infrastructure
- Create, update, and delete resources
- Assume roles across accounts

Most Terraform failures are **IAM failures in disguise**.

---

## Recommended baseline pattern

### One Terraform deployment role per environment
Examples:
- terraform- deploy- dev
- terraform- deploy- test
- terraform- deploy- prod

Each role:
- Has narrowly scoped permissions
- Is assumed via STS
- Is environment- specific

Never reuse a single role for all environments.

---

## Provider + IAM relationship

Terraform itself:
- Does not authenticate
- Relies entirely on the AWS provider

IAM controls:
- What Terraform can see
- What Terraform can change

See:
- [[Terraform AWS Provider]]
- [[AWS IAM Deep Dive]]

---

## Common IAM permissions Terraform needs

Almost every setup requires:
- sts:AssumeRole
- iam:PassRole (often forgotten)
- Read permissions for existing resources

Missing iam:PassRole is one of the **most common blockers**.

---

## Multi- account Terraform pattern

Typical flow:
1. CI/CD authenticates
2. Terraform assumes environment role
3. Provider alias targets correct account

Key rule:
> Terraform state, credentials, and permissions must all align to the same account boundary.

---

## Pitfalls (real- world)

❌ Using AdministratorAccess “temporarily”  
❌ Terraform works locally but fails in CI  
❌ IAM resources blocked by SCPs  
❌ Hardcoded account IDs  
❌ Overly broad wildcard policies  

---

## Best practices

- Explicit assume_role blocks
- Provider aliases for clarity
- Separate IAM bootstrapping from infra code
- Review IAM changes like code (PRs)

---

# AWS IAM Deep Dive

This note expands on [[AWS IAM Fundamentals]] and focuses on **how IAM actually behaves in practice**.

---

## Mental model (start here)
IAM answers exactly two questions:

1. **Who are you?**  
2. **What are you allowed to do?**

Everything else (users, roles, policies, STS) exists to answer those two questions safely and at scale.

---

## Identities in IAM

### IAM Users
- Long- lived credentials
- Represent humans
- Should be avoided for automation

**Best practice**
- Use IAM users only for:
  - Break- glass access
  - Very limited human access
- Enforce MFA always

---

### IAM Roles (preferred)
- No long- lived credentials
- Assumed temporarily
- Used by:
  - EC2
  - Lambda
  - CI/CD pipelines
  - Cross- account access

> If something is automated, it should use a **role**, not a user.

---

## Policies (the real core)

### Policy types
- **Identity- based policies** (attached to users/roles)
- **Resource- based policies** (attached to resources like S3)

### Policy structure
Policies are JSON documents defining:
- Actions
- Resources
- Conditions
- Effect (Allow / Deny)

**Key rule**
> Explicit deny always wins.

---

## Trust vs Permission Policies (critical distinction)

### Trust Policy
- Answers: **Who can assume this role?**
- Used only during role assumption

Example:
- EC2 service
- Another AWS account
- OIDC provider (GitHub Actions)

---

### Permission Policy
- Answers: **What can the role do once assumed?**
- Controls actual AWS actions

⚠️ Mixing these two up is one of the most common IAM mistakes.

---

## STS & Temporary Credentials

### AWS STS (Security Token Service)
- Issues short- lived credentials
- Used when assuming roles

### Why this matters
- Limits blast radius
- Enables cross- account access
- Required for modern CI/CD

Most AWS access today is:
> **AssumeRole → Temporary credentials → API calls**

---

## Cross- Account Access (common in real setups)

### How it works
1. Account A defines a role
2. Role trust policy allows Account B
3. Account B assumes the role
4. Temporary credentials are issued

### Typical use cases
- Central CI/CD account
- Shared Terraform deployment account
- Security tooling

---

## Service Control Policies (SCPs)

### What they are
- Guardrails at the AWS Organization level
- Apply to entire accounts or OUs

### What they are NOT
- They do NOT grant permissions
- They only restrict what *can* be granted

Think of SCPs as:
> “Even if IAM allows it, this is forbidden.”

---

## Conditions (advanced but powerful)

Policies can include conditions like:
- IP address
- MFA presence
- Time of day
- Source service

Example use cases:
- Force MFA for sensitive actions
- Restrict access to CI/CD IP ranges

---

## Common IAM Failure Modes (real- world)

- `AccessDenied` even though policy looks correct  
  → Often missing trust relationship

- Terraform works locally but fails in CI  
  → Different role, different permissions

- Everything works until SCPs are added  
  → SCP denies silently override IAM

- Overuse of `AdministratorAccess`  
  → Masks missing permissions and causes bad habits

---

## IAM Best Practices (battle- tested)

- Prefer roles over users
- Use least privilege
- Separate environments by account
- Enforce MFA everywhere
- Rotate credentials if users exist
- Log everything (CloudTrail)

---

## Terraform relevance

IAM is:
- One of the hardest Terraform domains
- Order- sensitive
- Easy to misconfigure

Common Terraform patterns:
- One IAM module per concern
- Explicit outputs for role ARNs
- Avoid inline policies for complex setups

See also:
- [[Terraform IAM Modules]]
- [[Terraform AWS Provider]]

---

## When to revisit this note
- CI/CD authentication fails
- Cross- account access breaks
- Security reviews
- Terraform refactors

IAM (Identity and Access Management) controls **who can do what** in AWS.

## Core building blocks
- **Users**: Human identities
- **Roles**: Assumable identities (preferred)

- **Groups**: User collections

- Define allowed or denied actions
- Always evaluated explicitly

- Roles are safer
- Roles scale better
- Roles are preferred for automation

## Trust vs Permission policies
- **Trust policy**: Who can assume the role
- **Permission policy**: What the role can do

## Common pitfalls
- Over- permissive policies (`*:*`)
- Hardcoded credentials
- Confusing trust and permission policies

# AWS Networking Decision Tree

Goal: choose a VPC architecture pattern quickly.

## Decision tree

1) **Single team, single app, early stage?**
- Yes → **Single VPC, multi- AZ, public+private subnets**
- No → go to 2

2) **Multiple environments (dev/test/prod) needing isolation?**
- Yes → **Separate AWS accounts** + VPC per account (preferred)
- No → VPC per environment (acceptable), but guardrails matter

3) **Multiple teams/apps needing shared services (DNS, tooling, inspection)?**
- Yes → **Hub- and- spoke** with a shared networking VPC
- No → go to 4

4) **Need many VPC- to- VPC connections or growth expected?**
- Yes → **Transit Gateway** (plan early)
- No → **VPC peering** (keep it small)

## Notes
- Favor **account separation** over “one huge VPC” when possible.
- Design CIDRs for growth: changing later hurts.

# AWS Organizations & SCPs

This note explains **how AWS Organizations and Service Control Policies (SCPs)** are used to enforce guardrails across accounts.

---

## AWS Organizations (what it is)
A service that allows you to:
- Group AWS accounts
- Centralize billing
- Apply organization- wide restrictions

The **account** remains the main isolation boundary.

---

## Service Control Policies (SCPs)

### What SCPs do
- Define the *maximum* permissions an account can ever have
- Apply to accounts or Organizational Units (OUs)

### What SCPs do NOT do
- They do NOT grant permissions
- They only restrict what IAM can allow

Think:
> IAM allows, SCPs veto.

---

## Why SCPs matter for Terraform & CI/CD

Terraform may:
- Have correct IAM permissions
- Still fail due to SCP denies

This often causes confusing `AccessDenied` errors.

---

## Common SCP use cases

- Prevent deleting CloudTrail
- Block root user actions
- Enforce region restrictions
- Block IAM user creation
- Require encryption

---

## CI/CD guardrail pattern

Typical setup:
- SCPs enforce non- negotiables
- IAM roles grant specific permissions
- CI/CD operates safely within bounds

This allows:
- Autonomy
- Safety
- Predictable behavior

---

## Common failure modes

- Terraform fails only in org- managed accounts
- SCP silently denies IAM permissions
- Overly aggressive SCP blocks automation

Always check SCPs when debugging IAM.

---

## Best practices

- Keep SCPs simple
- Document intent clearly
- Test SCPs in non- prod first
- Never use SCPs for fine- grained access control

---
